**The public-proof screen (round-5 repair of R4-1; R5-1/R5-2/R5-3).**
Published as `audits/evidence/retrofit/r1-public-proof-screen.py` with its
output `r1-public-proof-screen.out`. *Erratum:* the round-4 run tested
whether a source proof was contained **whole** in its counterpart, but the
round-4 text described "segments ≥ 60 characters". The round-5 auditor ran
the method as described and found six fragment hits that the containment
test could not see. The method below is the one actually run.

- **Method.** Strip comments and all whitespace. Rename each source
  identifier `h` to `f2_h` wherever Catalog declares `f2_h` (dotted names
  split). Report two measures:
  - the **longest common contiguous segment** (LCS), with the literal ≥ 60
    candidate threshold;
  - the **shared length**: greedy string tiling with blocks of at least 25
    characters, as a fraction of the **source** proof.
- **Rule.** A pair is a **member** when at least half of the source proof
  reappears in the target, with an absolute floor of 60 shared characters
  so that a one-line citation of a public lemma counts as reuse. Any other
  shared tiling of at least 60 characters is a recorded **fragment**, not
  counted. The rest are citations or no match.
- **Population (R5-3).** 17 eligible pairs: 2 from Composition (`id`,
  `const`) and **15** from Primitives, not the 16 stated in round 4. Five
  source theorems have no `_spaceUsed` counterpart: `ifEq`, `comp`,
  `splitSolveWith`, `unaryToken`, `appendBit`.
- **Pass 1, direct pairs.**
  - Members (7): `id` 96.5%, `const` 97.1%, `prepend` 93.9%,
    `pairEncodeFixed` 100%, `pairFst`/`pairSnd` 88.8%, `pairConcat`
    88.7%.
  - Fragments, recorded and not counted (3): `polyUnary` (119 characters
    shared, 46.7%); `pairLenCheck` (305, 21.9%; its LCS is the 91-character
    `Nat.pow_one` bound); `stripLast` (221, 11.7%; its LCS is the
    121-character `have hn` weakening).
  - Citations or no match (7): `lengthBits`, `polyBits`, `pairValid`,
    `pairDup`, `pairMapSnd`, `splitSolve` (the auditor's 27-character
    citation), `incFixed`.
  - The literal ≥ 60 LCS screen reproduces the auditor's hit set exactly
    (`id` 776, `const` 273, and 62/75/75/75/91/121 for the six Primitives
    pairs). One member falls below the 60-character LCS threshold:
    `pairEncodeFixed`, whose longest block is 53 characters but whose whole
    91-character source proof reappears. This is why the rule measures
    coverage, not contiguity alone.
- **Pass 2, residual helpers.** Each of the 27 nonmembers recorded in
  round 4 is screened against every public proof of Composition,
  Primitives and TimeConstructible, taking the best match by shared length.
  - Members (2): `f2_strip_linear` (86.0% of `computesFunInTime_stripLast`;
    R5-1) and `f2_counter_heads` (64.1% of `timeConstructible_id`; the
    auditor's 215-character partial-reuse candidate, which crosses the
    member bar once measured by tiling).
  - Fragments, recorded (6): `f2_counter_count_space` 6.5%,
    `f2_unary_sharp` 35.7%, `f2_cond_time` 30.0% (vs
    `bufferedCompTM_computesInTime`, a candidate the auditor did not list),
    `f2_rewind_scan_heads` 7.4%, `f2_rewind_heads` 6.0%,
    `f2_cond_ledger` 11.7%.
  - The remaining 19 share under 60 characters with any public proof.
- **Round-6 repair (R6-1, R6-5): pass 3, exhaustive.** Round 6 found
  R6-1, which the public-only residual pass could not see. Pass 3 replaces
  that scope limit. **Every one of Catalog's 124 non-members** (all of
  Catalog minus the post-R6-1 299-member union, computed by name in the
  script) is screened against **every declaration, public and private, of
  Composition, Primitives, TimeConstructible, Loop and Wrappers** (553
  declarations, of which 542 have an extracted body of at least 25
  characters; the other 11 cannot reach the 60-character floor). An exact 25-character prefilter is used; it loses nothing,
  because every tile is at least 25 characters. Verdicts compare like with
  like, proof with proof and term with term, so a proof that spells out a
  definition's term is reported as a restatement and not counted. **Every**
  qualifying pair is printed, not just each target's best match (R6-5).
  - Result: **19 cross-file members**, all counted in the Catalog row
    above. *Round-7 correction:* the round-6 text derived the source side
    from each target's best match only, giving "6 new source-side members"
    (R7-1). Pass 4 below replaces that hand step.
  - Five A2 members reproduce just over half of one 129-character Loop
    proof, `emLoop_run_prefix`. They are counted, as the rule requires,
    and flagged as low-coverage.
- **Round-7 repair (R7-1, R7-2): pass 4 generates the census.** No
  per-file member count is assembled by hand any more. **Pass 4** runs the
  like-kind rule over **all 423 Catalog declarations**, not only the
  non-members, against all five source files: 537 like-kind MEMBER pairs.
  **Every** pair's source joins its file's member set, together with the
  historical rules, stated by name in the script: f2_-twins, the
  `a2_loop_halted_run` twin, the relocation family, the 13 H3 copies, the
  counter block and `catalog_` twins. The script prints each file's count
  and every member beyond the historical rules, with spans. The rows above
  quote it.
  - Pass 4 reproduces the auditor's R7-1 additions (`controlCfg_run`,
    `emCall_right_run`, `exists_emitLoopTM`).
  - It also finds **24 further source-side members** (Primitives 16, Loop
    7, Wrappers 1). These are source declarations that a Catalog twin of a
    *sibling* declaration reproduces by more than half, so their material
    is duplicated in Catalog. Two of them are Loop's H3 near-copies
    `emLoopHost_init` and `emLoopHost_anchor_return`, previously
    "noted, uncounted"; they are now counted through the cross-file path.
  - Catalog is unchanged at 318.
  - **R7-2:** the body extractor now handles equation-style definitions and
    inductives (text from the first depth-0 `|` or `where`). The population
    labels are exact: 553 source declarations, 542 with an extracted body
    of at least 25 characters; the other 11 are genuinely shorter. Pass 3b
    carries the kind guard: **107 like-kind in-file pairs over 62 targets
    (12 at 90% or more), plus 2 restatements** (`f2_cond_ledger` ~
    `f2_timedReadyCfg`, `a2_loop_prepare` ~ `f2_loopReady`).
- **The membership rule in one sentence.** A declaration is a member when
  it is a historical twin or copy, or when it is either side of a
  like-kind cross-file pair in which at least half of the source's
  extracted body, and at least 60 characters, reappears in the target. The
  **exception** is in-file near-duplicates, which are recorded (pass 3b)
  and not counted; in-file exact copies are counted.
- **Standing in-file convention, stated explicitly.** Pass 3b lists
  in-file near-duplicates among the non-members: **109 raw printed
  pairs, of which 107 are like-kind, over 62 targets**. Twelve like-kind
  pairs reach 90%, and the other 2 are kind-mismatched restatements. They
  are led by the §12 sibling
  machine rows (`transferTM` against `copyTM` 99.8%, and the
  clear/compare/increment rows), which are public constructions audited at
  the §12 and F1 gates. Per the ledger's standing convention, which counts
  in-file **exact** copies (the H3 thirteen, the `a2_mapSumEquiv`/
  `a2_map_sum` pair) and **notes in-file near-duplicates without counting
  them**, they are recorded, not counted. None is an exact copy. Their
  disposition is the 12.2c per-theme split, which factors these families.
  An in-file near-match alone never adds a member. A declaration can still
  be a member independently through a cross-file pair: Loop's
  `emLoopHost_init` and `emLoopHost_anchor_return` count because their
  Catalog twins reproduce them.
- **Coverage qualification.** The screen covers the five source files of
  Catalog's copy families, in full, at the stated thresholds. Copies from
  files outside those families, or adaptations restructured below the
  25-character tile size, are outside it.

Copy-side counts deliberately include copies whose originals were deleted
in R1 (the copies persist; deletion of an original does not shrink the
copy side). The Loop inventory's recorded dispositions — the 8 dead
Loop-twin copies in Catalog (`f2_loop_silent_prefix`,
`f2_loopBody_capture`, the six `f2_loopDebit*`/`f2_loopBorrow*`) and the
orphans' dead twins — are **dispositions for 12.2c, not subtractions
here**; sole-owner/dead labels require Catalog's reference graph and are
settled at that window. Internal near-duplicates flagged by the
inventories but outside the rule (`clCountTape ≡ bufferTape`) are noted,
uncounted. The H3 `_init` pair, once in this list, counts since round 7
through its cross-file Catalog correspondence.

**Epoch R1 delta**: new copies **0**; the historical maps lost **eleven
dead originals plus one live original eliminated by replacement**
(`catalogPair_inverse`, the human-approved E1) — 245 → 233 surviving

## ===== campaign/items/c1/nf/NF-route-design.md =====

# NF: the linear normal form's route, before its brief (design note, maintainer, 2026-10-27)

**What this is for.** NF is `Turing.FinNDTM.exists_codeNDTM_accepts_linear`
(`ClassNP/NDNormalForm.lean:78`), one of the two contracts `Complexity.ntime_hierarchy` rests on
since #172 (the other is E-D's `exists_diagonalizer`). It is in its own module, so its fill can run
beside E-Q's and E-D's. Megafill D's triage (T3) found it blocked on the controller-stopped
writer's contract (the user's ruling of 2026-10-17). That contract was drafted
(`campaign/items/c1/nf-writer/WriterControllerDraft.lean.txt`) and never landed. This note
re-checks the C1 design's route (`C1-design.md` §2.4, steps N1–N7) against the tree, and fixes
what lands before the brief. Its decisions are at the end. It starts from the docstring's sketch:
guess the display, then verify it in `k + 1` sweeps.

**The statement** (frozen). For every `N : FinNDTM Bool` there are `M : CodeNDTM` and `C` with:
- forward, `N.AcceptsWithin x t → M.toFinNDTM.AcceptsWithin x (C * (t + 1))`;
- backward, `M.toFinNDTM.AcceptsWithin x t → ∃ t', N.AcceptsWithin x t'`.

`CodeNDTM` fixes **two** binary work tapes and states `Fin (numStates + 1)` (`NDCodes.lean:99`).
`AcceptsWithin x t` is a choice word of length exactly `t` whose run halts with output `[true]`
(`ClassNP/NTIME.lean:96`). The backward direction is unbounded and claims no all-branch halting,
so runaway guesses may run forever.

## What is published (at the tip `43fe918f`, Lean `940671e0`)

- **The choice writer** `Turing.ndWriterTM k j q₀ δ stop bounded` (`Build/NDHost.lean:203`), the
  definition of both flavors. Only the bounded flavor has a contract:
  `ndWriterTM_run_block` (`:351`), with the trivial controller over a nonblank block of `m` cells,
  every word of length `m + 1` reaching `done` at the same time. The controller-stopped flavor
  (`bounded := false`, a real `stop`) has **no contract**. The draft's statement is
  `ndWriterTM_run_controller`: if the controller first stops after `m` written bits, the prefix
  `w.take (m + 1)` writes `w.take m` from the head and reaches `done`, and no prefix of length at
  most `m` does. Its proof generalizes the bounded proof's private helpers (`wr_cfg` from `Unit`
  to any `Q`, with state `run ((w.take i).foldl δ q)`; `wr_tape_append` is `Q`-independent).
- **The guess-then-run host** `Turing.guessRunTM` (`:538`), with `guessRunTM_runWith`,
  `_haltsWithin` and `_accepts_iff` (`:1013`). **It composes only the bounded writer**, whose block
  length `m` the deterministic setup fixes before the guess. NF's display has length `W · t` for an
  unknown `t`, so `guessRunTM` cannot carry it. Its lemmas assume the bounded writer's synchronized
  timing (every branch guesses for exactly `m + 1` steps), so a controller-stopped variant needs
  its own run and acceptance lemmas. E-D's route cites `guessRunTM` as it is, so the variant is
  added beside it, not by changing it.
- **The phase hosts**: `Turing.NDTM.phaseHostND` with `phaseHostND_run` (`:93`, `:143`) for the
  nondeterministic composition, and `Turing.phaseHostTM` (`Build/Seam`) for the deterministic
  verifier's phases.
- **Rewinds and steps**: `skipTM`, `skipBackTM` (`Build/Catalog`), as `toNDTM` in the host.
- **The output summary**: `outputSummary`, `summaryEmit` and their laws (`Build/StepBlock.lean:142–198`),
  public, for sweep 0's check that the output is exactly `[true]`.
- **The packaging**: `Turing.NDTM.relabelState` with `relabelState_runWith`
  (`TuringMachine/Nondeterministic.lean:474, 488`), for the `Fin (numStates + 1)` states.
- **The run algebra**: `NDTM.runWith_nil`, `_cons`, `_append`, `runWith_of_halt`,
  `AcceptsWithin.mono`, `acceptsWithin_iff`, `MultiTapeTM.toNDTM`'s run equations, and the
  deterministic `step_of_some` and `Action.apply_*` field equations for own leaves.
- **Not usable here, but models:** StepBlock's public fixed-field reader `recordTM` and its
  `recordTM_effect` (the universal machine's H2 record, on `k + 2` tapes: a record tape, a summary
  cell and a mirrored bank). NF has two tapes in all, so its sweeps are new leaves.

## The shape (recommended)

`M` is the controller-stopped guess-then-run variant on tape A (tape 0). It guesses, rewinds A
and runs a deterministic two-tape verifier `V`, followed by the verdict bit. All of it is
relabeled into `Fin`.

**The display.** One record per step of `N`, of fixed width `W = 2k + 4`:
- the choice bit `bᵣ`;
- the `k + 1` claimed reads `σᵣ` (the input's and each work tape's), each `Option Bool` in a
  2-bit block;
- the end flag `endᵣ`.

**The guess** (N1). The controller is `Q := Fin W × Bool` (the position in the record, and
whether the last completed record carried the end flag). It stops at a record boundary after an
end-flagged record. A branch that never sets the flag never stops, which the statement allows.

**The verifier `V`** (deterministic, tapes A and B, the native input head). It runs these phases
under `phaseHostTM`, each followed by a rewind of A by `skipBackTM`:
1. **Sweep 0** (N2), a finite-state scan of A. It tracks `N`'s state from `q₀` and recomputes
   `aᵣ := N.tm.tr bᵣ qᵣ σᵣ` (the per-step actions are recomputed, never guessed). It checks that
   `endᵣ` is set exactly when `aᵣ` halts. It tracks the output summary through `summaryEmit`, and
   rejects unless the summary at the end is `[true]`'s.
2. **Sweep 1** (N3): the input claims. Each record's recomputed action moves the native input
   head; the claimed input read must equal the cell under it. Then the input head returns to its
   start, by a fixed seek (`exists_inputSeekTM`) or by reversing the recorded moves.
3. **Sweeps 2 … k + 1** (N4), one per work tape `j`. Tape `j` is replayed on B as 2-bit blocks
   `(visited, symbol)`, so that the visited region is contiguous and nonblank. B's head follows
   tape `j`'s claimed head (a move of `d` cells is `2d` cells on B). Each claimed read is checked
   against B's block, and the recomputed write is applied. Then B is cleared over the visited
   region and its head returned.
4. **The verdict**: accept iff every sweep passed.

Each sweep is one own-file finite-state leaf. It is a single machine reading A one cell per step,
with its run lemma by induction over records through `step_of_some`, not a private loop driver.

**The ledger.** The guess takes `W · t` steps for `t` records. Each sweep and rewind takes
`O(W · t)`, B's replay `O(W · t)` and its clear `O(W · t)`. In all `M` runs within
`C_N · (t + 1)`, with `C_N = O(k · W)`; the `+ 1` covers `k = 0` and `t = 0`.

**The transfers** (N6), each by induction on records:
- **Forward:** an accepting run of length `t₀ ≤ t` gives its display, `t₀` records with the flag on
  the last. The word that guesses it passes every sweep within `C_N (t₀ + 1)`; pad it to exactly
  `C · (t + 1)` (`runWith_of_halt`).
- **Backward:** a passing display is a genuine run. If the claimed reads up to `r − 1` are
  genuine, so are the recomputed actions, so each replayed tape at `r` is genuine, so sweeps 1 to
  `k + 1` make `σᵣ` genuine. The run halts at the flagged record with output `[true]`, so
  `N.AcceptsWithin x t'` holds with `t'` the record count.

**The packaging** (N5): the host's state type is finite, since every phase's is. Relabel it by
`Fintype.equivFin` into `Fin (card − 1 + 1)`, through `relabelState` and `relabelState_runWith`.

## What lands before the brief

**A maintainer API PR in `Build/NDHost`**, additive (no existing statement changes):
1. `ndWriterTM_run_controller`, the drafted contract, proved by generalizing the bounded proof's
   helpers (the B5a and H precedent of a maintainer landing in place of a fill).
2. **The controller-stopped guess-then-run host**, beside `guessRunTM`. It has the same phases,
   with the controller writer on a blank tape and no setup block. It needs a handoff lemma at the
   word-dependent guess time and an acceptance lemma: some word of length exactly `B` accepts iff
   some stopped stream makes `V`'s first verdict `acc` with an empty output, at every `B` beyond
   the run's time. There is no all-branch halting lemma; NF claims none.

It needs its gate, and a replay of `NDHost`'s downstream closure.

**Then NF's brief** owns `ClassNP/NDNormalForm.lean`: the record layout, the verifier's leaves,
the transfers and the packaging. It can run beside E-Q cont1 and E-D (different files). Its first
edit is the imports the API PR's rows need.

## Leaves and sizes (ESTIMATE)

| Piece | Where | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| The controller contract | the API PR (`NDHost`) | 100–200 |
| The controller guess-run host and its lemmas | the API PR (`NDHost`) | 400–700 |
| The record layout and its encoders and decoders | NF | 150–300 |
| Sweep 0, sweep 1, the tape sweep (parameterized by `j`), B's clear | NF | 1,200–2,500 |
| The verifier's phase composition | NF | 200–400 |
| The transfers, forward and backward | NF | 500–1,000 |
| The packaging and the ledger | NF | 150–300 |

The API PR is **0.5–0.9k**, and NF **2.2–4.5k** (the C1 plan's 2.5–5k for both).

## Copy hazards the brief names

- `ClassNP/ExhaustiveReplay` (`xr_` privates: replays of a fixed NDTM on a choice word), and
  `Nondeterminism`'s private `choiceCore` replay: run decompositions to cite or to avoid copying.
- `Build/StepBlock`'s `recordTM` and B5a's private `h1*` record family (`CodeSimulator`): models
  for a fixed-width reader, not citable on two tapes.
- `Build/NDHost`'s private `wr_*` helpers: the API PR generalizes them in place, so the fill
  never needs them.
- TR-1's truncation copies (`campaign/duplication-ledger.md`), if the transfer truncates an
  acceptance.

## Decisions

1. **The controller contract** (the 2026-10-17 ruling was a statement PR, then a W continuation
   to fill it).
   - (A) **Land it proved, by the maintainer API PR above. Recommended:** it is a small induction
     on the bounded proof's own helpers, in their own file, and saves a fill round.
   - (B) Keep the ruling: a statement PR, its gate, then a fill.
2. **Where the controller guess-run host lives.**

## What this is

**The linear-overhead coded normal form** ([AB09, §3.2]; [BGW70]-style guess-then-verify). For
every `N : FinNDTM Bool` there are `M : CodeNDTM` and `C` with
- **forward**, `N.AcceptsWithin x t → M.toFinNDTM.AcceptsWithin x (C * (t + 1))`;
- **backward**, `M.toFinNDTM.AcceptsWithin x t → ∃ t', N.AcceptsWithin x t'`.

`CodeNDTM` fixes **two** binary work tapes and the states `Fin (numStates + 1)`
(`TuringMachine/NDCodes.lean:99`). `AcceptsWithin x t` is a choice word of length **exactly** `t`
whose run halts with output **exactly** `[true]` (`ClassNP/NTIME.lean:96`; read it through
`Turing.FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_iff`). The backward direction is unbounded and claims no all-branch
halting: a runaway guess may run forever. `C` depends on `N` only.

**Where it stands.** Nothing of it is proved. The host it needs landed in PR #174 at the
maintainer's API gate (gate 85), proved, together with the controller's contract, so that this fill
writes the display, the verifier and the transfers, and composes nothing at the host level.

**Proved modulo, exactly:** none. **A complete delivery has no `sorryAx` in the target.**

### Hosts (binding; the host-first rule, `policy.md` §1, `workflow.md` §2)

- **`M` is the controller-stopped instance of the host**, relabeled:
  `guessCtlRunTM P pexit 0 q₀ δ stop false V qentry acc rej` with `k = 2` (tape `0` is A, the
  display; tape `1` is B, the replay tape), packaged into a `CodeNDTM` by
  `Turing.NDTM.relabelState` along `Fintype.equivFin`. Never compose `phaseHostND` yourself, never
  write a second writer, and never re-prove a handoff, a stop or an acceptance lemma of the host.
- **The setup `P` is trivial**: a two-tape machine whose start state is its exit `pexit`, so
  `TP = 0`. The route probe's `nfr_setup` proves the host's five setup hypotheses for it at time
  `0` on every tape (`runFrom_zero`, `initCfg_eq` and `Cfg.init`'s field equations); copy it as the
  private `nf_setup`.
- **The packaging** is the route probe's `nfr_pack`: for any finite-state `H : NDTM 2 Bool S`, some
  `M : CodeNDTM` has `M.toFinNDTM.AcceptsWithin x t` iff some choice word of length `t` halts `H`
  from `H.initCfg x` with output `[true]`. Copy it as the private `nf_pack` (keep its proof: it
  reads `toFinNDTM` through `CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM_tm`, `_k`, `_State`, and the relabeling through
  `relabelState_q₀` and `relabelState_runWith`). The host's state type is finite and has decidable
  equality by the published instances (`GuessRunPhase.instFintypeCtlState`,
  `instDecidableEqCtlState`), given those of its fibers: `V`'s state type, and so the fold's and the
  leaf's, must be a `Fintype` with `DecidableEq` (hold a record as `Fin _ → Option Bool`, not a
  list).
- **The verifier `V`** is a deterministic two-tape machine composed by `Turing.phaseHostTM`
  (`Build/Seam`, with `phaseHostTM_run`, `_run_le`, `_q₀`, `_tr_of_red_none`, `_tr_of_red_some`)
  over the published rows `Turing.scanTM` (sweep 0: `scanTM_run_ofCfg`, `scanFold`, `scanKeep`,
  `scanResult_fold`), `Turing.skipTM` and `Turing.skipBackTM` (`skipTM_run_ofCfg`,
  `skipBackTM_run_ofCfg`: the returns of A and B), `Turing.clearTM` (B's clear,
  `clearTM_run_ofCfg`; not the R3 row `clearTM_run`) and your one replay leaf. Its entry
  configuration is the host's `Turing.guessRunCfg cP 0 s qentry`: the stream `s` on A from cell
  `0`, A's head at `0`, B blank with its head at `0`, the input head at `1`, the output empty
  (read through the `guessRunCfg_*` field equations and `nfr_setup`'s configuration).
- **`V` is silent**: no leaf of `V` emits output. The host's verdict leaf emits the one bit.

### The route (binding where it names a row; the rest is the recommended shape)

**The display.** One record per step of `N`'s run, of fixed width `W = 2k + 4` (`k = N.k`): the
choice bit `bᵣ`; the `k + 1` claimed reads `σᵣ` (the input's, then each work tape's), each an
`Option Bool` in a 2-bit block; the end flag `endᵣ`. **The per-step actions are recomputed, never
guessed**: `aᵣ := N.tm.tr bᵣ qᵣ σᵣ`, with `qᵣ` tracked in each sweep's finite control.

**The guess** (ruling D3: a guessed end flag per record). The controller is `Q := Fin W × Bool` (the
position in the record, and whether the last completed record carried the end flag), with
`q₀ := (0, false)`, `δ (p, f) b := if p = W − 1 then (0, b) else (p + 1, f)` and
`stop (p, f) := (p = 0 && f)` (the flag is the record's last bit); `stop` holds exactly at a record
boundary after an end-flagged record. So a stopped stream is a sequence of
complete records whose last, and only last, record is end-flagged. A branch that never sets the flag
never stops; the statement allows it.

**`V`'s phases** (A's head is back at cell `0` after each):
1. **Sweep 0**, the control check, is **the published scan fold** on A:
   `Turing.scanTM 2 0 (scanFold δ₀) scanKeep a₀`, with your fold step `δ₀` over the stream's bits.
   From the entry it reaches `done (s.foldl δ₀ a₀)` at exactly `2|s| + 2`, no `done` earlier, with
   every tape and head as at the entry, so A needs no rewind (`scanTM_run_ofCfg`,
   `scanResult_fold`). `δ₀`'s state (a `Fintype` with `DecidableEq`) holds: the position in the
   record and the record read so far; `qᵣ`, from `N.tm.q₀`; the output summary, from
   `outputSummary [] = none` and updated by `summaryEmit`; a failure flag. At each record's end it
   recomputes `aᵣ` and checks that `endᵣ` is set exactly when `aᵣ.state = none`. Its verdict passes
   iff no check failed and the final summary is `some true` (`outputSummary_true`: exactly
   `[true]`). **Write no machine for sweep 0.**
2. **Sweep 1**, the input claims: each record's recomputed action moves the native input head
   (the same `SignType` move, so the same `moveInputPos`), and the claimed input read must equal
   the cell under it. The input head is not returned: no later phase reads the input, and the
   acceptance lemmas constrain only `V`'s state and output.
3. **Sweeps 2 … k + 1**, one per work tape `j < k`: tape `j` is replayed on B as 2-bit blocks, a
   visited cell as two nonblank bits encoding its `Option Bool` content and an unvisited cell as two
   blanks, so the visited region is contiguous and nonblank. B's head follows tape `j`'s claimed
   head (a move of one cell is two cells on B); each claimed read is checked against B's block, and
   the recomputed write is applied. Then B's head goes to the visited region's first cell and B is
   cleared, by three published rows on B: `skipTM` (over the region from B's head,
   `skipTM_run_ofCfg`; it leaves the head one past the region's right blank); `skipBackTM`
   (`u :=` the whole region, `skipBackTM_run_ofCfg`); `clearTM` (`clearTM_run_ofCfg`), which leaves
   B blank with its head at the region's first cell. The region is never empty: every record writes
   its block.
4. **The verdict:** `acc` iff every sweep passed; `rej` at the first failure.

**A's return after a replay sweep.** A replay sweep ends with A's head on the blank after `s`
(cell `|s|`). `skipBackTM_run_ofCfg` needs the head **one cell past** that blank, so first step
right with `skipTM` on A (`skipTM_run_ofCfg` at `w := []`), then run `skipBackTM` on A at
`u := s`, as the host does after its writer. `Build/Rewind`'s `rewindTM`, which starts on the
blank, is outside your imports.

**One leaf for sweeps 1 to `k + 1`.** They share the record scan and the recomputation: write one
leaf parameterized by the tape it replays (the input, or work tape `j` on B), not `k + 1` copies.
It is a single own-file machine reading A one cell per step (A stationary while it works on B),
with its run lemma by induction over records through `MultiTapeTM.step_of_some` and the
`Action.apply_*` field equations; no private loop driver. The sweeps are own-file leaves by the
design note (its "Leaves and sizes" table; D2 moved only the guess-run host to `Build/NDHost`):
their contract is this file's display format, and no other consumer exists.

**Recommended shape.** State each leaf's run lemma as "after `r` records, a pure fold of the
stream" (as `scanTM_run_ofCfg` does), and `V`'s lemma as a characterization: its first verdict at a
time `T(s)`, `acc` iff every fold passes. That one lemma gives `hV`, the forward `hacc` and
`hfirst`, and the backward "accepted ⇒ every check passed"; the transfers then never touch a
machine.

**`hV`, the backward lemma's obligation (binding):** for **every** stream `s` that first stops the
controller at its end, well formed or not in content, `V` reaches a verdict, `acc` or `rej`, from
`guessRunCfg cP 0 s qentry`, and is at neither before. Each replay sweep ends at the blank after
`s` or rejects earlier; B's replay moves its head at most two cells per record; and B's clear
(`skipTM`, `skipBackTM`, `clearTM`) runs over the visited region, which is contiguous and nonblank
on every stream. So `V` is total; prove it as a lemma of its own, not inside the backward
transfer.

**The transfers.**
- **Forward** (`guessCtlRunTM_accepts_of`): from `N.AcceptsWithin x t`, take its word, the first
  time `t₀ ≤ t` its run halts, and the display `s` of those `t₀` steps (`|s| = W · t₀`); `s` first
  stops the controller at its end (`hslive`, `hsstop`); `V` is at `acc` at `TQ` (`hacc`), at
  neither `acc` nor `rej` before (`hfirst`), with an empty output (`hnil`); `TQ = O(k · W · t₀)`;
  and the lemma gives a word of length exactly `C · (t + 1)` once
  `0 + 2 |s| + TQ + 11 ≤ C · (t + 1)`. `t₀ ≥ 1`, since the start state is live.
- **Backward** (`guessCtlRunTM_stream_of_accepts`, with `hV`): an accepting word of `M` gives a
  stopped stream `s` that `V` accepts with an empty output. By induction on records, a passing
  display is a genuine run: if the claimed reads before record `r` are genuine, so are the
  recomputed actions, so each replayed tape at `r` is genuine, so sweeps 1 to `k + 1` make `σᵣ`
  genuine. The run halts at the flagged record with output `[true]`, so `N.AcceptsWithin x t'`
  with `t'` the record count and the record bits as the word.

**The ledger.** `C := C_N`, uniform in `x` and `t`: each sweep and rewind is `O(W · t₀)`, B's
replay and clear `O(W · t₀)`, `V` in all `O(k · W · t₀)`, and the `+ 1` covers `k = 0` and the
constants.

**Edge cases that must stay true:**
- `N.k = 0`: no tape sweep; `V` is sweep 0, sweep 1 and the verdict, and `W = 4`;
- a run halting at its first step (`t₀ = 1`): one record;
- a run whose input head moves left of the first cell, or right past the input: the claimed read is
  the blank there, and `moveInputPos` is the machine's own move;
- a write of a blank (`some none`) on a work tape: the block encodes `none`, and the cell stays
  visited;
- the output: a halting transition may emit (`summaryEmit` covers it); a run emitting twice is
  rejected (`some false` is irreversible);
- a stream whose claims are wrong: `V` rejects it, and still reaches its verdict (`hV`);
- a claimed-read block with the unused fourth code: sweep 0 rejects it (or it decodes to `none`;
  say which in `REPORT.md`).

## Known pitfalls at this pin (hard-won)

- **The simps field equations are pointwise** (`Cfg.init_workTapes`, `guessRunCfg_workTapes`,
  `Cfg.mapState_workTapes` take the tape and the cell): `funext i p` before `rw`, or the step
  closes by unfolding and the seal rejects it.
- **`CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM`'s fields are dependent** (`k`, `State`, `tm`): read them together by
  `simp only [CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM_tm, CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM_k, CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM_State]` (as
  `nf_pack` and `NDCodeSimulator` do), not one by one with `rw`.
- **`AcceptsWithin` is exact length.** The forward lemma gives a word of length exactly `B`; choose
  `B := C * (t + 1)` and prove the lower bound `2 |s| + TQ + 11 ≤ B`.
- **The acceptance lemmas hide the word:** the forward one returns it, and the backward one returns
  the stream; never build or split a choice word yourself.
- **Under the seal, never write a host state yourself** (`⟨.pre, P.q₀⟩`, `Sigma.mk .run`): with
  `GuessRunPhase.CtlState` sealed, `CtlState SP SQ Q .run` does not reduce. Cite only
  `guessCtlRunTM_accepts_of` and `guessCtlRunTM_stream_of_accepts`, whose statements name none.
- **`guessCtlRunTM_stop_of_halted` is the backward lemma's first step**, already inside
  `guessCtlRunTM_stream_of_accepts`: cite the latter, not both.
- **No core or Mathlib definition is reduced outside `rfl`, `decide` or `show`**: write
  `congrArg (fun b => [b])`, not `congrArg List.singleton`. Recursive definitions get usage
  controls, not delta controls.
- `omega` with products as atoms (`ring` first). The linter needs a literal "Proof sketch" before
  every `sorry` (partial only).

## What this is

**The linear-overhead coded normal form** ([AB09, §3.2]; [BGW70]-style guess-then-verify). For
every `N : FinNDTM Bool` there are `M : CodeNDTM` and `C` such that:
- **forward**, `N.AcceptsWithin x t → M.toFinNDTM.AcceptsWithin x (C * (t + 1))`;
- **backward**, `M.toFinNDTM.AcceptsWithin x t → ∃ t', N.AcceptsWithin x t'`.

`CodeNDTM` fixes two binary work tapes. `AcceptsWithin x t` asks for a choice word of length
**exactly** `t` whose run halts with output **exactly** `[true]`; read it through

### The route (binding where it names a row or a pin; the rest is the recommended shape)

**V's layout (pinned; the route probe).** Copy the probe's layout as your own privates under the
`nf_` prefix: the phase index (`NfcPh` there), the state family, the named instances, the
machines, the redirect table and the verifier. The phases, in order:
1. the control sweep;
2. the input's replay, then A's return (`skipTM` on A at `w := []`, then `skipBackTM` on A at
   `u := s`);
3. for each work tape `j < k`: its replay on B; A's return; then B's clear (`skipTM` on B over the
   visited region's suffix from B's head, `skipBackTM` on B with `u :=` the whole region, then
   `clearTM_run_ofCfg` on the region);
4. the verdict park.

`nfc_aReturn` is A's return chained through `phaseHostTM_run`, `nfc_retag` the step from a
redirected configuration to the next phase's start. Keep both, renamed. `nfc_aReturn` is stated
for the input's return: state it once for every replayed tape, whose last redirect is
`nfcAfter N L none` for the input and `⟨.bFwd j, .run⟩` for work tape `j`. A layout of equal
strength is allowed if you say why in `REPORT.md`, for example the leaf's verdict exits read
through another function than the probe's `exit : SL → Option Bool`. **B's clear (pinned):**
`rv_bClear` (`NFContClearTail.lean.txt`) chains the phases `bFwd j`, `bBack j` and `bClr j`
through `phaseHostTM_run` from B's head at any offset `i ≤ |R|` into a blank-delimited region `R`
(`i = |R|`, the right delimiter, included), ending with B blank on the region and B's head on its
first cell. Keep it, renamed.

**Named instances (pinned).** As in the probe: `DecidableEq` and `Fintype` for the phase family's
fibers (`nfcStDecEq`, `nfcStFintype`), with the control sweep's `ScanPhase (nf_SweepState N)`
inside them (`@instDecidableEqScanPhase _ inferInstance`, `@instFintypeScanPhase _ inferInstance`),
and for the leaf's state, each as a `private instance` (or `local instance`). `V`'s state then has
both by inference (the probe's two `example`s). Default synthesis does not reach
`DecidableEq (ScanPhase (nf_SweepState N))` at the default instance size (the review's F3). Never
raise `synthInstance.maxSize` instead.

**The replay leaf (pinned).**
- **One own-file two-tape machine, parameterized by the replayed tape** (`none` the input,
  `some j` work tape `j` on B), not `k + 1` copies.
- **It reads every claim through `nf_decode`** (MP5). This is what makes `01 ↦ blank` sound for the
  backward direction.
- **It reads A one cell per step,** keeps A stationary while it works on B, and recomputes each
  record's action `N.tm.tr bᵣ qᵣ σᵣ` in its finite control.
- **The input instance** compares each decoded input claim with the cell under the native input
  head, then performs the recomputed input move (`moveInputPos`). The input head is not returned.
- **A work-tape instance** keeps tape `j` on B as two-bit blocks: a visited cell is two nonblank
  bits encoding its `Option Bool` content, an unvisited cell two blanks. B's head sits at its
  start position plus twice the simulated head, so a simulated move is two cells on B. It checks
  each decoded claim against B's block, then **writes the block at every record**: two nonblank
  bits encoding the cell's content after the step, `(a.workTapes j).1.getD old` (the shape of
  `Action.apply_workTapes`). An action that writes nothing (`(a.workTapes j).1 = none`) still
  writes its block, so an unvisited cell under the head becomes the nonblank code of blank.
  Otherwise the visited region can have blank holes, and B's clear either does not apply or leaves
  cells that a later work tape's replay reads, rejecting a genuine display.
- **Its exits** are a pass state, entered after the end-flagged record with A's head on the blank
  after `s` (cell `|s|`, not past it: `nfc_aReturn`'s `hpos`), or a reject state.
- **Its run lemma** has the shape "after `r` records, a pure fold of the stream". It is framed over
  A's position, with the stream read from A's head; B's head position, with B blank or holding the
  region; and the input position. It gives the exact time as a function of the stream. Prove it
  by induction over records through `MultiTapeTM.step_of_some` and the `Action.apply_*` field
  equations; no private loop driver.
- **The exit invariant on B (pinned).** At a work-tape instance's exit, B is blank outside the
  visited region, which is nonempty, contiguous and nonblank (every record writes its block), and
  B's head is on a cell of it. B's clear also applies from the region's right delimiter, but not
  from the block left of the region: there `skipTM_run_ofCfg` at `w := []` ends on the left
  delimiter, and `skipBackTM_run_ofCfg` at `u :=` the region does not apply. Since every record
  writes its block, the head can leave the region only by the last record's move, and only a
  move to the left is harmful. **Keep the invariant by not performing the end-flagged record's
  head move** (pinned, user 2026-11-04): the leaf knows the record is the last when it completes
  it, and that move affects no later check. The region is then exactly the blocks read. If the
  work tape's head never moves, the region is the one block at B's start.

`NFReviewProbe.lean.txt`, `rv_tag` and `rvPark` from `NFReviewVProbe.lean.txt`, and this round's
`nfc_retag`, `nfc_aReturn` and `rv_bClear`, as `nf_pack` and `nf_setup` were; renamed `nf_`):
- `rv_entry`: `V`'s entry is `streamStartCfg x 0 q s`;

**`hV`, the backward lemma's obligation (binding).** For **every** stream `s` that first stops the
controller at its end, well formed or not in content, `V` reaches a verdict, `acc` or `rej`, from
`guessRunCfg cP 0 s qentry`, and is at neither before. Prove it as a lemma of its own, not inside
the backward transfer. Why it holds:
- the control sweep runs on every stream (`nf_sweep_run`);
- each replay ends at A's blank after `s`, or rejects earlier;
- B's replay moves its head at most two cells per record;
- B's clear runs over the visited region, which is contiguous, nonblank and holds B's head by the
  exit invariant.

**Recommended shape.** State `V`'s lemma as a characterization: its first verdict at a time
`TQ(s)`, `acc` iff every fold passes. That one lemma gives `hV`, the forward `hacc` and `hfirst`,
and the backward "accepted ⇒ every check passed". The transfers then never touch a machine.

**The transfers.**
- **Forward** (`guessCtlRunTM_accepts_of`):
  - from `N.AcceptsWithin x t`, cut its word at the first halting time `t₀ ≤ t` (`t₀ ≥ 1`);
  - the display `s` of those `t₀` steps (`|s| = W · t₀`) gives `hslive` and `hsstop`
    (`nf_display_firstStop`);
  - the control sweep passes (`nf_sweep_display_pass`) and every replay passes, so `hacc`,
    `hfirst` and `hnil` hold;
  - the lemma's exact budget is `C · (t + 1)`.
- **Backward** (`guessCtlRunTM_stream_of_accepts`, with `hV`):
  - work over raw records' decoded fields, never over `nf_record` images, since `01` also decodes
    to blank;
  - split the stopped stream by `nf_firstStop_records` and a product-index law (as
    `nf_display_records` does), then apply `nf_sweep_records`;
  - by induction on records, passed checks make every decoded read genuine, hence every
    recomputed action genuine;
  - the flagged record halts, with output `[true]`, so `N.AcceptsWithin x t'`, with `t'` the
    record count and the records' choice bits as the word.

**The ledger (pinned shape).** `0 + 2|s| + TQ(s) + 11 ≤ C · (t + 1)`, with `|s| = (2k + 4) · t₀`,
`t₀ ≤ t`, and `TQ(s)` the sum of the phase times:
- the control sweep, `2|s| + 2`;
- each replay, `O(|s|)`, with `O(1)` B operations per record;
- each return of A, `|s| + 6`, its two redirects included (`nfc_aReturn`);
- each clear of B, `(|R| − i + 1) + (|R| + 3) + (2|R| + 2)` with `R` the region and `i` B's
  head's offset in it, plus its three redirects: `4|R| − i + 9 = O(t₀)`;
- one step for each other redirect (after the control sweep and after each replay).

`C` is a closed form in `N.k`, uniform in `x` and `t`. Give it term by term in `REPORT.md`.

**Edge cases that must stay true:**
- `N.k = 0`: no work-tape phase. After the input's return the redirect goes to the verdict
  (`nfcAfter none`), and `W = 4`;
- `t₀ = 1`: one record;
- the input head left of the first cell or past the input: the claimed read is the blank there;
- a work-tape write of a blank: the block encodes `none` and stays nonblank;
- a work-tape action that writes nothing: its block is still written, so the region has no hole;
  a work tape whose head never moves: the region is one block;
- a halting transition that emits (`summaryEmit`), or a run emitting twice (rejected by the
  control sweep);
- wrong claims: rejected, and the verdict still reached (`hV`);
- the code `01`: decoded as blank (`nf_decode_absent`).

## Known pitfalls at this pin (hard-won)

- **Named instances, not default synthesis** (above): `DecidableEq (ScanPhase (nf_SweepState N))`
  fails at the default instance size, and so does anything built over it (`Σ i, …`, the host's
  fibers).
- **A redirected configuration is the next phase's start only up to `mapState`.**
  `phaseHostTM_run` ends at `c'.mapState (fun _ => q')`. Rewrite it with the probe's
  `nfc_retag` into `c''.mapState (Sigma.mk i)` before the next `phaseHostTM_run`, as
  `nfc_aReturn` does.
- **`skipTM_run_ofCfg` reads `w` and then one blank.** From A's blank after `s`, use `w := []`.
  Its result is one cell right, as `skipBackTM_run_ofCfg` at `u := s` needs.
- **The simps field equations are pointwise** (`Cfg.init_workTapes`, `streamStartCfg_workTapes`,
  `Cfg.mapState_workTapes`): use `funext i p` before `rw`.
- **`AcceptsWithin` is exact length.** Choose `B := C * (t + 1)` and prove `2|s| + TQ + 11 ≤ B`.
- **The acceptance lemmas hide the word:** the forward one returns it, and the backward one returns
  the stream. Never build or split a choice word yourself.
- **Under the seal, never write a host state yourself.** With `GuessRunPhase.CtlState` sealed,
  `CtlState SP SQ Q .run` does not reduce. Cite only `guessCtlRunTM_accepts_of` and
  `guessCtlRunTM_stream_of_accepts`.
- **No core or Mathlib definition is reduced outside `rfl`, `decide` or `show`.** Recursive
  definitions get usage or equation controls, not delta controls.
- `omega` treats products as atoms (`ring` first). The linter needs a literal "Proof sketch" before
  every `sorry` (partial only).

## Completed construction and declarations

Checkpoint 2 implements sweep zero as a finite bit fold and proves its record-prefix, whole-record, multi-record, genuine-run, and scan laws. It proves that a display whose branch first halts at its end with output `[true]` passes the control check. It does not yet verify the input or work-tape claims.

The record width is `W = 2 * N.k + 4`. Slot 0 is the branch choice; read `i`, input first,
uses slots `2*i+1` and `2*i+2`; slot `2*N.k+3` is the end flag. Presence/value codes are
`00` for blank, `10` for false, and `11` for true. `nf_decode` maps the unused `01` code to blank; `nf_decode_absent` proves this choice.

`nf_display N x w` encodes the read configuration before each choice in `w`. It sets only
the last record's flag. It is defined for every word, not only accepting or first-halting
words; the forward transfer must still select the first-halting prefix before using it.
States and actions are not recorded or guessed.

The controller has type `Fin W × Bool`: position and last completed flag. It resets to
position zero and stores the bit on the final slot; otherwise it increments the position.
It stops exactly at position zero with a true saved flag.

## Edge cases and remaining obligations

| Edge case | Status after checkpoint 2 |
|---|---|
| `N.k = 0` | All width/record/controller lemmas are uniform; width is 4 and positive. No work-tape indexing is assumed nonempty. |
| One-step halt | The nonempty-display first-stop theorem applies to a singleton word. Sweep zero acceptance follows from `nf_sweep_display_pass`; full verifier acceptance remains open. |
| Input at either blank boundary | The display records `Cfg.inputSymbol` itself. The input-replay comparison remains open. |
| Work-tape write of blank | Record format supports the blank read. Visited-block replay semantics remain open. |
| Emission on halt, or twice | `nf_complete_output` and `nf_complete_step` include the halting emission; `nf_complete_other` and `nf_sweepPass_output` handle irreversible rejection and exact singleton output. |
| Incorrect claims | The controller theorem and the scan-run theorem apply to arbitrary content. Sweep zero always finishes; rejection of wrong tape claims and totality of the full verifier remain open. |
| Unused fourth read code | `nf_decode` and `nf_decode_absent` implement and prove decoding `01` as blank. |

No constant `C` has been established. The required ledger still has to bound the host's
`2*|s| + TQ + 11` by `C*(t+1)`, with `|s| = (2*N.k+4)*t₀` and `t₀ ≤ t`. Sweep zero is now proved to cost exactly `2*|s|+2`. The guess/rewind
contribution, input replay/return, all work replays/returns/clears, the verifier's
redirects, and the host's `+11` must all appear in that bound. This report does not supply
an unproved numerical value of `C`.

The following are **proposed continuation declarations, not declarations admitted in the
source**. Each names an open obligation and its Proof sketch.

1. **Checkpoint 3 — `nf_replayTM` (common replay-leaf definition, not implemented).**
   **Proof sketch.** Define one finite-state leaf parameterized by input versus work-tape
   index. Reuse the finite record decoder and action recomputation; move A only while
   reading its record, and keep it fixed during B's block operations. The leaf's docstring
   must distinguish it from the one-tape scan and StepBlock's `k+2`-tape record reader.
2. **Checkpoint 3 — `nf_replay_input_run`.**
   **Proof sketch.** Compare each decoded input claim with the native input head, then
   perform the recomputed input move. Induct on records via `step_of_some` and the action

## Proposed target-docstring paragraph (not landed)

**Implementation.** A controller guesses a display with one fixed-width record per step:
the choice bit, the input and work-tape reads, and an end flag. The state and transition are
recomputed in finite control. A silent deterministic verifier uses the published scan fold
for the control and output checks, then one shared replay leaf for the input and each work
tape, with the published rewind and clear routines between sweeps. The controller-stopped
guess-run host emits the verdict, and finite-state relabeling packages it as a two-work-tape
code. The present partial development establishes the display, controller, setup, packaging,
and sweep-zero control check, including its verdict on first-halting accepting displays;
the replay sweeps, full verifier, and acceptance transfers remain to be proved.

**The replay leaf:**

| Declaration | Role |
|---|---|
| `nf_LeafSt` | the leaf's states: `read σ` (σ the control sweep's own parser and control), `blk₁`/`blk₂` on the block of tape `1`, `adj₁`/`adj₂` (two head adjustments), `pass`, `rej` |
| `nf_leafEquiv`, `nf_leafStDecEq`, `nf_leafStFintype` | an equivalence with a sum of finite types, and the leaf state's **`private instance`s** through it (each summand's instance given locally: default synthesis does not reach the sum at the default size) |
| `nf_act` | the action of `N`'s table on a completed record's decoded claims (the action `nf_complete` recomputes) |
| `nf_blockDecode` | a two-cell block of tape `1` decoded as `nf_decode` decodes a claim (`01` and blank to blank) |
| `nf_leaf` | **the replay leaf**, one machine parameterized by `j : Option (Fin N.k)`; its docstring names the rows it is not (`scanTM` reads one tape; `StepBlock`'s record reader reads records on `k + 2` tapes). Every action is a `Turing.tapeAction` |
| `nf_leafExit` | the exit reader: `pass ↦ some true`, `rej ↦ some false` |

The leaf reads tape `0` one cell per step through `nf_sweepStep` (the control sweep's parser and
control, so its simulated state is the control fold's by construction). At a record's last bit
it decodes the record through `nf_decode` (MP5) and recomputes `N.tm.tr` (`nf_act`). The input
instance compares the decoded input claim with the native input cell and performs the recomputed
input move (`moveInputPos`, through the action), in the same step that reads the last bit; it
does not return the input head. A work-tape instance then works on tape `1` with tape `0`
stationary: `blk₁` reads the block's first cell and writes the first bit of the new content,
`blk₂` reads the second cell, checks `nf_blockDecode` against the claim, and writes the second
bit; the content is `(a.workTapes j).1.getD claim`, written at **every** record; then the head of
tape `1` moves `+1` or `−1` and `adj₁`, `adj₂` move it `0` or `−1` each, so the simulated move is
two cells. **After the end-flagged record the head move is skipped** (the leaf passes from
`blk₂`, its head on the block's second cell), as pinned.

| `nf_forward` | **the forward transfer**: `N.AcceptsWithin x t →` a word of length exactly `C(t + 1)` halts the host with output `[true]` (the word is the host lemma's: `guessCtlRunTM_accepts_of`; no word is built here) |

**Checkpoint 7: the backward transfer:**

| Declaration | Role |
|---|---|
| `nf_backward` | a stream of records on which every check passes is a genuine accepting run: `nf_allPass N x rs → N.AcceptsWithin x rs.length`, with the records' choice bits as the word (through `nf_vrun_of_ok`); it works over raw records' decoded fields (`nf_decode`), never over `nf_record` images |
| `nf_backward_host` | **the backward transfer**: a word halting the host with output `[true]` gives `∃ t', N.AcceptsWithin x t'`, through `guessCtlRunTM_stream_of_accepts` with `hV` (`nf_hV`), `nf_split`, and the characterization (its first verdict is the host lemma's `TQ`, since both are first verdicts) |

**Checkpoint 8: the target** (region (c)):

```lean
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := nf_pack (nf_host N)
  refine ⟨M, nf_C N.k, fun x t hN => (hM x _).2 (nf_forward N x t hN), fun x t hMt => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨w, -, hh, ho⟩ := (hM x t).1 hMt
  exact nf_backward_host N x w hh ho
```

`M` is the controller-stopped host (`nf_host`) packaged by `nf_pack`; `C = nf_C N.k`.

**`C`, term by term** (`n = t₀` records, `|s| = W t₀`, `W = 2k + 4`):

| Term | Steps | Bound used |
|---|---|---|
| the trivial setup `TP` | `0` | `0` |
| the guess (the host's `2|s|`) | `2|s|` | `2W t₀` |
| the control sweep and its dispatch | `2|s| + 2 + 1` | |
| the input's replay and its dispatch | `W t₀ + 1` | |
| the return of tape `0` after the input (two redirects included) | `|s| + 6` | the three: `4|s| + 10` |
| per work tape: its replay and dispatch | `(2k + 8)t₀ − 2 + 1` | |
| per work tape: the return of tape `0` | `|s| + 6` | |
| per work tape: the clear of tape `1` (three redirects included) | `(|R| − i + 2) + (|R| + 4) + (2|R| + 3) ≤ 4|R| + 9`, `|R| ≤ 2t₀` | per tape `≤ (2W + 12)t₀ + 15` |
| the host's constant | `11` | `11` |

Total `0 + 2|s| + TQ + 11 ≤ (6W + k(2W + 12))t₀ + 21 + 15k ≤ C(t + 1)` since `t₀ ≤ t`.

The run lemmas are proved by induction over records through `Turing.step_of_tapeAction_move` (the
published one-step lemma of `Turing.tapeAction`, itself proved from `MultiTapeTM.step` and the
`Action.apply` field equations), with no private loop driver.

### Semantic duplication: the search per new private

Three searches for every new declaration (`evidence/final/`):
1. **By name**, in the tree and on every branch and PR head of the remote (306 refs: all
   `refs/heads/*` and `refs/pull/*/head`, fetched; a superset of the open PRs, since the GitHub API is
   not enabled for this session): `git grep -w` of each of the 64 names: **no occurrence outside the
   owned file** for any of them.
2. **By statement shape**, the same refs, `git grep -E` of each lemma's characteristic pattern
   (`evidence/duplication/semantic-grep.txt`, with every hit).
3. **By `exact?`**, at the module's imports, for every lemma whose statement mentions no definition
   of this file (`evidence/duplication/NFExactProbe.lean`, `exact-probe.log`: every `exact?` reports that it
   could not close the goal). A lemma whose statement mentions this
   file's definitions (the leaf, its states, the phases, `nf_decode`, the control fold, the virtual
   run, the block representation) cannot be stated by a published declaration, which cannot see
   them; for those the shape search is the semantic search.

| Declaration(s) | Shape searched | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `nf_Ph`, `nf_St`, `nf_stDecEq`, `nf_stFintype`, `nf_park`, `nf_M`, `nf_after`, `nf_red`, `nf_V` | the pinned layout (the route probe's, renamed) | the probe's own layout; no published verifier over these rows |
| `nf_LeafSt`, `nf_leafEquiv`, `nf_leafStDecEq`, `nf_leafStFintype`, `nf_leaf`, `nf_leafExit`, `nf_act`, `nf_blockDecode`, `nf_blockWrite` | readers of fixed-width records checked against another tape; two-bit block codes (`blockDecode`, `blockWrite`, "two-bit block") | none: `scanTM` reads one tape; `StepBlock`'s and `CodeSimulator`'s record readers read `k + 2` tapes; the "two-bit block" hits (`Randomized/Build/PairSplit`, `UnaryMul`, `Build/Catalog`) are parsers of aligned `00`/`11` words, not a replayed tape |
| `nf_retag` | `theorem …retag`; redirected configuration as a tagged start | none public; `SeamLayout`'s **private** `sl_rewrap` states it for its own family: **promotion request** |
| `nf_tagged_ne_park` | `(c.mapState (Sigma.mk i)).state ≠ …` | none public; `CfgRecord`'s **private** `record_tag_ne` is a generalization: **promotion request** |
| `nf_aNext`, `nf_aReturn`, `nf_bClear` | `skipBackTM_run_ofCfg` chains on two tapes | `Build/RecordTable` chains `skipBackTM` inside its own record table (a different composition); the authorized transcriptions of the route probe and the review's `rv_bClear` |

| `nf_tag` | `streamStartCfg … mapState (Sigma.mk …)` | none (the review's `rv_tag`, for this family) |
| `nf_inputSymbol_congr` | `inputSymbol = ….inputSymbol`, `…inputSymbol_congr` | `ExhaustiveReplay`'s **private** `xr_inputSymbol_congr` states it; the other hits are `rfl` facts of particular configurations: **promotion request** (as the brief lists it); `exact?`: none |
| `nf_prefix_last`, `nf_leaf_prefix`, `nf_leaf_record_in`, `nf_leaf_run_in`, `nf_leaf_block`, `nf_leaf_record_wk`, `nf_leaf_run_wk` | run lemmas of this file's leaf | none possible elsewhere (the leaf is this file's); they cite `nf_sweep_prefix`, `nf_sweep_record` and the published one-step lemmas of `tapeAction` |
| `nf_vstep`, `nf_ok`, `nf_vstep_state`, `nf_vstep_ctl`, `nf_vrun_ctl`, `nf_vrun_genuine` | `Fin.cases c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols`; decoded runs | none: the first round's `nf_complete_step` and `nf_sweep_control_prefix` are about the control fold on genuine records; these are about the decoded virtual run on arbitrary records |
| `nf_stream_cons`, `nf_stream_length`, `nf_split`, `nf_all_cons`, `nf_flags_cons` | `flatMap List.ofFn` and its length | none in TCSlib; `exact?`: none `exact?`: none `exact?`: none |
| `nf_blocks`, `nf_blocks_decode`, `nf_blocks_write`, `nf_blocks_support`, `nf_region` | block representations of a tape; a region read off as a buffer | none; `exact?`: none |
| `nf_signType_bound` | `(m : ℤ) ≤ 1` for `SignType` | none in TCSlib; `exact?`: none |
| `nf_tapeEntry`, `nf_allPass`, `nf_allPass_iff`, `nf_V_tail`, `nf_V_char`, `nf_hV`, `nf_V_display` | the verifier's characterization | none possible elsewhere (this file's verifier) |
| `nf_P`, `nf_host`, `nf_C`, `nf_ledger`, `nf_forward`, `nf_backward`, `nf_backward_host` | first halting time (`Nat.find … runWith`, "first halting"); the transfers | `EXP`'s private `enumCont_first_halt` and `SAT`'s, `ExhaustiveReplay`'s, `ConfigCount`'s first-halting arguments are about other runs; `nf_forward` cuts its word with `Nat.find` inline, as no published lemma states the first halting time of an `NDTM` branch; the transfers are the host's acceptance lemmas, cited |

## 8. Checklist

- [x] Preflight numbers, roots (39), cache fetch (1,007 of 1,007; store empty before), the store's
      log, the logs in this zip (`evidence/logs/`), the bootstrap with per-module time and memory,
      the base blob check (§1).
- [x] Nothing outside regions (b)–(d); the 39 privates and the target's statement unchanged (the
      diff's four hunks, §2; it deletes only the base's `sorry` and the two status phrases).
- [x] Checkpoints 3–8, one commit and one zip each; the base hash and the ancestor check (§1, status).
- [x] Every new declaration with its role (§2): the leaf and its run lemmas, the exit invariant (the
      skipped last move), the instances, `V`'s phases and redirects, the hand-built machine's
      docstring naming the rows it is not.
- [x] `hV` as its own lemma (`nf_hV`), and the edge cases: `N.k = 0` (`nf_tapeEntry … 0` is the
      passing verdict and `nf_V_tail` runs zero tapes; `W = 4`); `t₀ = 1` (one record:
      `nf_leaf_run_in`/`_wk`'s base case, `nf_split`); the input head off the input (the claim is
      compared with `Cfg.inputSymbol`, blank there: `nf_inputSymbol_congr`); a work-tape write of a
      blank and an action writing nothing (`(a.workTapes j).1.getD claim`, always written:
      `nf_leaf_block`, `nf_blocks_write`); a work tape whose head never moves (the region is one
      block: `nf_blocks_write` from `[0, −1]`); a halting transition that emits, or two emissions
      (the control sweep's summary, first round, rejects; `nf_V_char`); wrong claims (rejected,
      verdict still reached: `nf_V_char`, `nf_hV`); the code `01` (`nf_decode`, MP5:
      `nf_backward` works over decoded fields).
- [x] `C`, term by term (§2): the guess, the control sweep, each replay and return, the clears, the
      redirects, the host's `+ 11`.
- [x] The base sorry list by name (§1), and the final sweep's (§6).
- [x] Promotion requests and escalations (§5); the `**Implementation.**` paragraph needs no change.
- [x] Rule 10 (§3): the cited declarations from the elaborated-constant walk; the probe re-run (908
      checks of 751 names); the seal with its 231 discriminating controls and both raw outputs; the
      inspection table.
- [x] Rule 11 (§3): no R3 row, no other file's private; the two derived instance names checked.
- [x] Duplication (§7): both screens (and the superseded first after screen), every new pair with a

## 9. What is in this zip

- `REPORT.md`; `source/` (the owned file at `825ee3f5`); `patches/` (`git format-patch` of the 7
  commits on the base); `bundle/` (a bundle of `fill/c1-nf-cont1` whose only prerequisite is the
  base, with `git bundle verify`'s output); `SHA256SUMS`.
- `evidence/logs/`: preflight, restart re-check, cache store, roots, cache fetch, manifest check,
  cache probe, the bootstrap and the final sweep (logs, per-module tables, sorry lists), the

- `evidence/checks/`: the tail, the walk, the axiom prints (`NFAxioms.lean`, `axioms-raw.log`),

- `evidence/seal/`: the sealed module copy, the seal set, the sealed/unsealed control sources and

- `evidence/duplication/`: the shape search, the name search, the `exact?` probe and its output,

- `evidence/runtime/`: the scripts used for the checks (sweep, walk, seal, probe, inspection, zip).

## ===== campaign/fills/c1/evidence/c1-nf-cont1/checks/NFAxioms.lean.txt =====

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.NTIME
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.NDCodes
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.NDHost
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.StepBlock

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The linear-overhead coded normal form of an NDTM

[AB09, §3.2] ([BGW70]-style guess-then-verify): every bundled binary nondeterministic machine has a
coded two-work-tape equivalent (`Turing.CodeNDTM`) whose acceptance tracks the original's at linear
time overhead, forward with an explicit constant and backward in unbounded form. The
nondeterministic time hierarchy (`TCSlib.Complexity.Diagonalization.NTimeHierarchy`) diagonalizes
over these codes. This module isolates the normal-form statement and its supporting construction.

## Main definitions

No new definitions: the normal form is an existential contract.

## Main results

* `Turing.FinNDTM.exists_codeNDTM_accepts_linear` — the linear-overhead coded normal form.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§3.2.)
* [BGW70] R. Book, S. Greibach, B. Wegbreit, *Time- and tape-bounded Turing
  acceptors and AFLs*, JCSS 4(6), 1970. (Cited through [AB09]; no external text is required.)
-/

namespace Turing

namespace FinNDTM

/-- A finite-state machine with two binary work tapes has a code with identical acceptance.

**Proof sketch.** Relabel the finite state type by its equivalence with a finite ordinal.
Read the initial configuration and the relabeled run through their field equations, and
transfer halting and the exact output word in both directions. -/
private theorem nf_pack {S : Type} [Fintype S] (H : NDTM 2 Bool S) :
    ∃ M : CodeNDTM, ∀ (x : List Bool) (t : ℕ), M.toFinNDTM.AcceptsWithin x t ↔
      ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = t ∧ (H.runWith w (H.initCfg x)).state = none ∧
        (H.runWith w (H.initCfg x)).output = [true] := by
  have hpos : 0 < Fintype.card S := Fintype.card_pos_iff.mpr ⟨H.q₀⟩
  let e : S ≃ Fin (Fintype.card S - 1 + 1) :=
    (Fintype.equivFin S).trans (finCongr (by omega))
  refine ⟨⟨Fintype.card S - 1, H.relabelState e⟩, fun x t => ?_⟩
  rw [FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_iff]
  simp only [CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM_tm, CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM_k, CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM_State]
  have hinit : (H.relabelState e).initCfg x = (H.initCfg x).mapState e := by
    rw [NDTM.initCfg_eq, NDTM.initCfg_eq, NDTM.relabelState_q₀]
    apply Cfg.ext
    · rw [Cfg.init_state, Cfg.mapState_state, Cfg.init_state]; rfl
    · rw [Cfg.init_inputPos, Cfg.mapState_inputPos, Cfg.init_inputPos]
    · funext i p; rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapes, Cfg.init_workTapes, Cfg.init_workTapes]
    · funext i; rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapePos, Cfg.init_workTapePos, Cfg.init_workTapePos]
    · rw [Cfg.mapState_output, Cfg.init_output, Cfg.init_output]
  rw [hinit]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨w, hw, hh, ho⟩
    refine ⟨w, hw, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [NDTM.relabelState_runWith, Cfg.mapState_state] at hh
      exact Option.map_eq_none_iff.mp hh
    · rwa [NDTM.relabelState_runWith, Cfg.mapState_output] at ho
  · rintro ⟨w, hw, hh, ho⟩
    refine ⟨w, hw, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [NDTM.relabelState_runWith, Cfg.mapState_state, hh]; rfl
    · rwa [NDTM.relabelState_runWith, Cfg.mapState_output]

/-- The trivial setup: a machine started at its exit meets `Turing.guessCtlRunTM`'s setup
hypotheses at time `0`, on every tape. -/
private theorem nf_setup {SP : Type} (P : MultiTapeTM 2 Bool SP) (z : List Bool) (j : Fin 2) :
    P.runFrom (P.initCfg z) 0 = P.initCfg z ∧ (P.initCfg z).state = some P.q₀ ∧
      (∀ u < 0, (P.runFrom (P.initCfg z) u).state ≠ some P.q₀) ∧
      (∀ p : ℕ, (P.initCfg z).workTapes j ((P.initCfg z).workTapePos j + p) = none) ∧
      (P.initCfg z).workTapes j ((P.initCfg z).workTapePos j - 1) = none := by
  refine ⟨MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, ?_, fun u hu => absurd hu (Nat.not_lt_zero u), fun p => ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [MultiTapeTM.initCfg_eq, Cfg.init_state]
  · rw [MultiTapeTM.initCfg_eq, Cfg.init_workTapes]
  · rw [MultiTapeTM.initCfg_eq, Cfg.init_workTapes]

/-- The display controller records the next position and the last completed record's flag. -/
private def nf_ctlStep (k : ℕ) (q : Fin (2 * k + 4) × Bool) (b : Bool) :
    Fin (2 * k + 4) × Bool :=
  if h : q.1.val = 2 * k + 3 then (0, b)
  else (⟨q.1.val + 1, by have := q.1.isLt; omega⟩, q.2)

/-- The controller stops precisely at a record boundary carrying a true end flag. -/
private def nf_ctlStop (k : ℕ) (q : Fin (2 * k + 4) × Bool) : Bool :=
  decide (q.1.val = 0) && q.2

/-- Starting at a record boundary, the position is the length read modulo the record width.

**Proof sketch.** Induct by appending one bit. At the last position the controller resets;
otherwise it advances by one. These are exactly the two cases of addition modulo the width. -/
private theorem nf_ctl_position (k : ℕ) (s : List Bool) (f : Bool) :
    (s.foldl (nf_ctlStep k) (0, f)).1.val = s.length % (2 * k + 4) := by
  induction s using List.reverseRecOn with
  | nil =>
    simp only [List.foldl_nil, List.length_nil, Nat.zero_mod]
    rfl
  | append_singleton s b ih =>
    simp only [List.foldl_append, List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_nil,
      List.length_append, List.length_singleton]
    rw [nf_ctlStep]
    split_ifs with h
    · have hm : s.length % (2 * k + 4) = 2 * k + 3 := by omega
      rw [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (show 1 < 2 * k + 4 by omega), hm]
      have he : 2 * k + 3 + 1 = 2 * k + 4 := by omega
      simp only [he, Nat.mod_self, Fin.val_zero]
    · have hp := (s.foldl (nf_ctlStep k) (0, f)).1.isLt
      have hm : s.length % (2 * k + 4) + 1 < 2 * k + 4 := by omega
      rw [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (show 1 < 2 * k + 4 by omega),
        Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hm]
      exact congrArg (fun n => n + 1) ih

/-- A nonempty prefix stops exactly when its length is a whole number of records and its
last bit is true.

**Proof sketch.** Separate the empty prefix and a prefix obtained by appending one bit.
The last position resets to zero and records that bit; every other position is nonzero. -/
private theorem nf_ctl_stop_iff (k : ℕ) (s : List Bool) :
    nf_ctlStop k (s.foldl (nf_ctlStep k) (0, false)) = true ↔
      s ≠ [] ∧ s.length % (2 * k + 4) = 0 ∧ s.getLastD false = true := by
  induction s using List.reverseRecOn with
  | nil => simp [nf_ctlStop]
  | append_singleton s b _ =>
    have hp := nf_ctl_position k (s ++ [b]) false
    rw [List.foldl_append, List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_nil, nf_ctlStep] at hp ⊢
    split_ifs at hp ⊢ with h
    · have hz : (s ++ [b]).length % (2 * k + 4) = 0 := hp.symm
      have hz' : (s.length + 1) % (2 * k + 4) = 0 := by
        simpa only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton] using hz
      simp [nf_ctlStop, hz']
    · have hn : (s ++ [b]).length % (2 * k + 4) ≠ 0 := by
        intro hz
        have hp' : (s.foldl (nf_ctlStep k) (0, false)).1.val + 1 =
            (s ++ [b]).length % (2 * k + 4) := hp
        omega
      have hn' : (s.length + 1) % (2 * k + 4) ≠ 0 := by
        simpa only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton] using hn
      simp [nf_ctlStop, hn']

/-- A record consists of its choice bit, two bits for each claimed read (input first), and
its end flag. A blank is encoded by `00`, false by `10`, and true by `11`. -/
private def nf_record (k : ℕ) (b : Bool) (reads : Fin (k + 1) → Option Bool) (last : Bool)
    (p : Fin (2 * k + 4)) : Bool :=
  if p.val = 0 then b
  else if h : p.val = 2 * k + 3 then last
  else
    let i : Fin (k + 1) := ⟨(p.val - 1) / 2, by have := p.isLt; omega⟩
    if (p.val - 1) % 2 = 0 then (reads i).isSome else (reads i).getD false

/-- The last position of a record is its end flag. -/
private theorem nf_record_last (k : ℕ) (b : Bool) (reads : Fin (k + 1) → Option Bool)
    (last : Bool) : nf_record k b reads last ⟨2 * k + 3, by omega⟩ = last := by
  rw [nf_record, if_neg (show 2 * k + 3 ≠ 0 by omega), dif_pos rfl]

/-- The first position of a record is its choice bit. -/
private theorem nf_record_choice (k : ℕ) (b : Bool) (reads : Fin (k + 1) → Option Bool)
    (last : Bool) : nf_record k b reads last 0 = b := by
  rw [nf_record, if_pos (show (0 : Fin (2 * k + 4)).val = 0 from rfl)]

/-- Each claimed read occupies its designated presence bit and value bit.

**Proof sketch.** At the two designated offsets the quotient is the claimed-read index.
The remainder distinguishes its presence bit from its value bit. -/
private theorem nf_record_read (k : ℕ) (b : Bool) (reads : Fin (k + 1) → Option Bool)
    (last : Bool) (i : Fin (k + 1)) :
    nf_record k b reads last ⟨2 * i.val + 1, by omega⟩ = (reads i).isSome ∧
      nf_record k b reads last ⟨2 * i.val + 2, by omega⟩ = (reads i).getD false := by
  have hi := i.isLt
  constructor
  · have hq : (2 * i.val + 1 - 1) / 2 = i.val := by omega
    have hr : (2 * i.val + 1 - 1) % 2 = 0 := by omega
    rw [nf_record, if_neg (show 2 * i.val + 1 ≠ 0 by omega),
      dif_neg (show 2 * i.val + 1 ≠ 2 * k + 3 by omega), if_pos hr]
    exact congrArg (fun j => (reads j).isSome) (Fin.ext hq)
  · have hq : (2 * i.val + 2 - 1) / 2 = i.val := by omega
    have hr : (2 * i.val + 2 - 1) % 2 ≠ 0 := by omega
    rw [nf_record, if_neg (show 2 * i.val + 2 ≠ 0 by omega),
      dif_neg (show 2 * i.val + 2 ≠ 2 * k + 3 by omega), if_neg hr]
    exact congrArg (fun j => (reads j).getD false) (Fin.ext hq)

/-- The display of a branch records the reads before each step, the step's choice bit, and
an end flag only on the last record. Actions and machine states are not guessed. -/
private def nf_display (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  List.ofFn fun i : Fin ((2 * N.k + 4) * w.length) =>
    let r : Fin w.length := ⟨i.val / (2 * N.k + 4),
      (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul (by omega)).2 (by simpa only [Nat.mul_comm] using i.isLt)⟩
    let p : Fin (2 * N.k + 4) := ⟨i.val % (2 * N.k + 4), Nat.mod_lt _ (by omega)⟩
    let c := N.tm.runWith (w.take r.val) (N.tm.initCfg x)
    nf_record N.k w[r.val] (Fin.cases c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols)
      (decide (r.val + 1 = w.length)) p

/-- A display has exactly `2k + 4` bits per step. -/
private theorem nf_display_length (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x w : List Bool) :
    (nf_display N x w).length = (2 * N.k + 4) * w.length := by
  simp only [nf_display, List.length_ofFn]

/-- The end bit of the `r`th record of a display is true exactly on its last record.

**Proof sketch.** With the width `W = 2k + 4`, the final cell of record `r` has index
`W(r+1)-1`. Its quotient by `W` is `r` and its remainder is `W-1`, so the record encoder returns
the prescribed end flag. -/
private theorem nf_display_flag (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x w : List Bool) (r : Fin w.length) :
    (nf_display N x w)[(2 * N.k + 4) * (r.val + 1) - 1]? =
      some (decide (r.val + 1 = w.length)) := by
  let W := 2 * N.k + 4
  have hW : 0 < W := by omega
  have hprod : 0 < W * (r.val + 1) := Nat.mul_pos hW (by omega)
  have hi : W * (r.val + 1) - 1 < (nf_display N x w).length := by
    rw [nf_display_length]
    have hle := Nat.mul_le_mul_left W (show r.val + 1 ≤ w.length by omega)
    show W * (r.val + 1) - 1 < W * w.length
    omega
  have hd : (W * (r.val + 1) - 1) / W = r.val := by
    simpa only [Nat.zero_add, Nat.zero_div, Nat.add_sub_cancel] using
      Nat.mul_sub_div 0 W (r.val + 1) hprod
  have hm : (W * (r.val + 1) - 1) % W = 2 * N.k + 3 := by
    have he := Nat.mod_add_div (W * (r.val + 1) - 1) W
    rw [hd] at he
    have hdecomp : W * (r.val + 1) = W * r.val + W := by ring
    rw [hdecomp] at he ⊢
    have he' : W = 2 * N.k + 4 := rfl
    omega
  rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem hi]
  simp only [nf_display, List.getElem_ofFn]
  have hp : (⟨(W * (r.val + 1) - 1) % W, Nat.mod_lt _ hW⟩ : Fin W) =
      ⟨2 * N.k + 3, by omega⟩ := Fin.ext hm
  rw [hp, nf_record_last]
  exact congrArg (fun a : ℕ => some (decide (a + 1 = w.length))) hd

/-- Every nonempty branch display first stops the controller exactly at its end.

**Proof sketch.** A stopping prefix must end on a record boundary. Its last bit is therefore
one of the display's end flags, which is false before the last record and true there. -/
private theorem nf_display_firstStop (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x w : List Bool) (hw : w ≠ []) :
    (∀ i < (nf_display N x w).length,
      nf_ctlStop N.k (((nf_display N x w).take i).foldl (nf_ctlStep N.k) (0, false)) = false) ∧
      nf_ctlStop N.k ((nf_display N x w).foldl (nf_ctlStep N.k) (0, false)) = true := by
  have hwpos : 0 < w.length := List.length_pos_iff.mpr hw
  have hW : 0 < 2 * N.k + 4 := by omega
  constructor
  · intro i hi
    apply Bool.eq_false_iff.mpr
    intro hs
    obtain ⟨hne, hm, hb⟩ := (nf_ctl_stop_iff N.k _).mp hs
    have hipos : 0 < i := by
      have hp := List.length_pos_iff.mpr hne
      rw [List.length_take, Nat.min_eq_left hi.le] at hp
      exact hp
    rw [List.length_take, Nat.min_eq_left hi.le] at hm
    have he := Nat.mod_add_div i (2 * N.k + 4)
    rw [hm, Nat.zero_add] at he
    have hn : 0 < i / (2 * N.k + 4) := by
      by_contra h
      have hnonneg : 0 ≤ i / (2 * N.k + 4) := Nat.zero_le _
      have hz : i / (2 * N.k + 4) = 0 := by omega
      rw [hz, Nat.mul_zero] at he
      omega
    have hlt : i / (2 * N.k + 4) < w.length := by
      apply (Nat.mul_lt_mul_left hW).mp
      rw [he, ← nf_display_length N x w]
      exact hi
    let r : Fin w.length := ⟨i / (2 * N.k + 4) - 1, by omega⟩
    have hr : r.val + 1 = i / (2 * N.k + 4) := by
      show i / (2 * N.k + 4) - 1 + 1 = i / (2 * N.k + 4)
      omega
    have hflag := nf_display_flag N x w r
    rw [hr, he, decide_eq_false (show ¬i / (2 * N.k + 4) = w.length by omega)] at hflag
    rw [List.getLastD_eq_getLast?, List.getLast?_eq_getElem?, List.length_take,
      Nat.min_eq_left hi.le, List.getElem?_take_of_lt (by omega), hflag,
      Option.getD_some] at hb
    exact Bool.noConfusion hb
  · apply (nf_ctl_stop_iff N.k _).mpr
    have hspos : 0 < (nf_display N x w).length := by
      rw [nf_display_length]
      exact Nat.mul_pos hW hwpos
    refine ⟨List.ne_nil_of_length_pos hspos, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [nf_display_length, Nat.mul_mod_right]
    · let r : Fin w.length := ⟨w.length - 1, by omega⟩
      have hr : r.val + 1 = w.length := by
        show w.length - 1 + 1 = w.length
        omega
      have hf := nf_display_flag N x w r
      rw [hr, decide_eq_true rfl] at hf
      rw [List.getLastD_eq_getLast?, List.getLast?_eq_getElem?, nf_display_length,
        hf, Option.getD_some]

/-- A stream that first stops the controller consists of a positive number of complete
records, with false end flags on all but the final record, whose end flag is true.

**Proof sketch.** The stopping criterion makes the total length a positive multiple of the
width. Apply the same criterion to each shorter record boundary: its flag must be false,
since a true flag there would contradict the first-stop hypothesis. -/
private theorem nf_firstStop_records (k : ℕ) (s : List Bool)
    (hlive : ∀ i < s.length, nf_ctlStop k ((s.take i).foldl (nf_ctlStep k) (0, false)) = false)
    (hstop : nf_ctlStop k (s.foldl (nf_ctlStep k) (0, false)) = true) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ s.length = (2 * k + 4) * n ∧
      ∀ r < n, s[(2 * k + 4) * (r + 1) - 1]? = some (decide (r + 1 = n)) := by
  obtain ⟨hsne, hmod, hlast⟩ := (nf_ctl_stop_iff k s).mp hstop
  have hspos := List.length_pos_iff.mpr hsne
  have hW : 0 < 2 * k + 4 := by omega
  let n := s.length / (2 * k + 4)
  have hlen : s.length = (2 * k + 4) * n := by
    have h := Nat.mod_add_div s.length (2 * k + 4)
    rw [hmod, Nat.zero_add] at h
    exact h.symm
  have hn : 0 < n := by
    by_contra h
    have hnonneg : 0 ≤ n := Nat.zero_le _
    have hz : n = 0 := by omega
    rw [hz, Nat.mul_zero] at hlen
    omega
  refine ⟨n, hn, hlen, ?_⟩
  intro r hr
  let m := (2 * k + 4) * (r + 1)
  have hmpos : 0 < m := Nat.mul_pos hW (by omega)
  have hmle : m ≤ s.length := by
    rw [hlen]
    exact Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega)
  have hib : m - 1 < s.length := by omega
  have hlasttake : (s.take m).getLastD false = s[m - 1] := by
    rw [List.getLastD_eq_getLast?, List.getLast?_eq_getElem?, List.length_take,
      Nat.min_eq_left hmle, List.getElem?_take_of_lt (by omega),
      List.getElem?_eq_getElem hib, Option.getD_some]
  rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem hib]
  by_cases he : r + 1 = n
  · have hm : m = s.length := by
      show (2 * k + 4) * (r + 1) = s.length
      rw [he, ← hlen]
    have htake : s.take m = s := by rw [hm, List.take_length]
    rw [htake] at hlasttake
    have hb : s[m - 1] = true := hlasttake.symm.trans hlast
    rw [hb, decide_eq_true he]
  · have hmlt : m < s.length := by
      rw [hlen]
      exact Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left (by omega) hW
    have hb : s[m - 1] = false := by
      apply Bool.eq_false_iff.mpr
      intro htrue
      have hniltake : s.take m ≠ [] := by
        apply List.ne_nil_of_length_pos
        rw [List.length_take, Nat.min_eq_left hmle]
        exact hmpos
      have hz : (s.take m).length % (2 * k + 4) = 0 := by
        rw [List.length_take, Nat.min_eq_left hmle]
        exact Nat.mul_mod_right _ _
      have hf := (nf_ctl_stop_iff k (s.take m)).mpr
        ⟨hniltake, hz, hlasttake.trans htrue⟩
      rw [hlive m hmlt] at hf
      exact Bool.noConfusion hf
    rw [hb, decide_eq_false he]

/-- Displaying the first `t` steps of a long enough branch uses exactly `(2k + 4)t` bits. -/
private theorem nf_display_prefix_length (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x w : List Bool) (t : ℕ)
    (ht : t ≤ w.length) : (nf_display N x (w.take t)).length = (2 * N.k + 4) * t := by
  rw [nf_display_length, List.length_take, Nat.min_eq_left ht]

/-- A record's claimed reads; an absent presence bit decodes to blank regardless of its
value bit. Thus the unused code `01` also decodes to blank. -/
private def nf_decode (k : ℕ) (r : Fin (2 * k + 4) → Option Bool)
    (i : Fin (k + 1)) : Option Bool :=
  if (r ⟨2 * i.val + 1, by omega⟩).getD false then
    some ((r ⟨2 * i.val + 2, by omega⟩).getD false)
  else none

/-- Decoding a displayed record recovers each claimed read. -/
private theorem nf_decode_record (k : ℕ) (b : Bool) (reads : Fin (k + 1) → Option Bool)
    (last : Bool) (i : Fin (k + 1)) :
    nf_decode k (fun p => some (nf_record k b reads last p)) i = reads i := by
  rw [nf_decode, Option.getD_some, Option.getD_some,
    (nf_record_read k b reads last i).1, (nf_record_read k b reads last i).2]
  cases reads i <;> rfl

/-- A false presence bit decodes to blank, including the unused fourth two-bit code. -/
private theorem nf_decode_absent (k : ℕ) (r : Fin (2 * k + 4) → Option Bool)
    (i : Fin (k + 1)) (h : (r ⟨2 * i.val + 1, by omega⟩).getD false = false) :
    nf_decode k r i = none := by
  rw [nf_decode, h]
  rfl

/-- The control check retains the simulated state, output summary, and an irreversible
failure flag. -/
private abbrev nf_Control (N : FinNDTM Bool) := Option N.State × Option Bool × Bool

/-- The sweep's finite control retains a position, a partially filled record, and its
control-check data. The record is a function on a finite type, never an unbounded list. -/
private abbrev nf_SweepState (N : FinNDTM Bool) :=
  (Fin (2 * N.k + 4) × (Fin (2 * N.k + 4) → Option Bool)) × nf_Control N

/-- Completing a record recomputes its action and checks its end flag. A record after
halting sets the failure flag. The summary includes emissions of halting transitions. -/
private def nf_complete (N : FinNDTM Bool) (r : Fin (2 * N.k + 4) → Option Bool)
    (c : nf_Control N) : nf_Control N :=
  match c.1 with
  | none => (none, c.2.1, true)
  | some q =>
    let reads := nf_decode N.k r
    let a := N.tm.tr ((r 0).getD false) q (reads 0) (fun j => reads j.succ)
    (a.state, StepBlock.summaryEmit c.2.1 a.output,
      c.2.2 || decide ((r ⟨2 * N.k + 3, by omega⟩).getD false ≠ a.state.isNone))

/-- The bit fold stores one bit, completing the record exactly at its last position. -/
private def nf_sweepStep (N : FinNDTM Bool) (c : nf_SweepState N) (b : Bool) :
