```
  refine ⟨t + (y.length + 2), c.inputPos, c.workTapes, c.workTapePos, by omega, ?_⟩
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, bufferedFirstCfg_init,
    bufferedFirstCfg_run M₁ M₂ _ t (fun s hs => Nat.find_min hh hs)]
  have hf := bufferedFirstCfg_rewind M₁ M₂ c hs
  cases ho
  exact hf

end Turing.FinTM

/-! ### Machine-agreement transfer (§13, Z5)

Two machines over the same tape count and state type whose transition
tables agree on a set of control states run identically for as long as the
run's control stays inside that set. This is the `hagree` genre of
`Turing.capture_run`/`Turing.emit_run` made standalone: those lemmas carry
a per-state agreement hypothesis for one specific wrapper, re-proved ad hoc
at every host; the standalone form transfers whole runs between any two
agreeing tables (design `machine-library-design.md` §13, item Z5; decision
D-R3). First customers: the forwarding loop host of `Build/Loop.lean`
(whose fourteen phase lemmas are verbatim re-proofs of the capturing
host's, since the two tables agree on every non-body state) and the
guarded `clSlot_run` agreement sites of `CookLevin/Hardness.lean`. -/

namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM

/-- The two transition tables agree on every control state in `Q`: from any
such state, both machines take the identical action on identical reads.
Nothing is assumed about states outside `Q`, about `q₀`, or about
halting. -/
def AgreeOn {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type*} (M N : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (Q : Set State) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ Q, ∀ inp work, M.tr q inp work = N.tr q inp work

/-- **The agreement, unfolded** (the ND inventory API, round 2; C1-WC's review): the tables agree
on `Q` iff `M.tr q inp work = N.tr q inp work` for every `q ∈ Q` and all reads. -/
theorem agreeOn_iff {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type*} (M N : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (Q : Set State) :
    M.AgreeOn N Q ↔ ∀ q ∈ Q, ∀ inp work, M.tr q inp work = N.tr q inp work :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- One step transfers across an agreement: if the configuration's control
state (when live) lies in the agreement set, both machines step it to the
same configuration. Halted configurations step to themselves on both sides.

**Proof sketch.** On `c.state = none` both steps are the identity. On
`c.state = some q` with `q ∈ Q`, unfold `step`: both sides apply the same
action `M.tr q c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols = N.tr q …` to `c`. -/
theorem step_eq_of_agreeOn {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type*}
    {M N : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State} {Q : Set State}
    (h : M.AgreeOn N Q) {input : List Symbol} (c : Cfg k Symbol State input)
    (hq : ∀ q, c.state = some q → q ∈ Q) :
    N.step c = M.step c := by
  cases hs : c.state with
  | none => simp only [step_of_halt hs]
  | some q =>
    simp only [step, hs]
    rw [h q (hq q hs)]

/-- A whole run transfers across an agreement: if every control state the
`M`-run visits strictly before time `t` lies in the agreement set, the two
runs coincide at time `t` (and hence at every earlier time, by
instantiating `t`). The endpoint itself may leave the set or halt; no
liveness is assumed, and `t = 0` is the trivial case.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on `t`. The inductive hypothesis transfers the
run at `t`; the visit hypothesis at `u = t` puts its live control in `Q`,
so `step_eq_of_agreeOn` transfers the final step. Halted intermediate
configurations step identically on both sides without the hypothesis. -/
theorem runFrom_eq_of_agreeOn {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type*}
    {M N : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State} {Q : Set State}
    (h : M.AgreeOn N Q) {input : List Symbol} (c : Cfg k Symbol State input)
    (t : ℕ) (hq : ∀ u < t, ∀ q, (M.runFrom c u).state = some q → q ∈ Q) :
    N.runFrom c t = M.runFrom c t := by
  induction t with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [runFrom_succ_eq_step', ih (fun u hu => hq u (by omega)),
      runFrom_succ_eq_step']
    exact step_eq_of_agreeOn h _ (hq t (by omega))

end Turing.MultiTapeTM
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/ChoiceReplay.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Nondeterministic
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Choice-tape determinization: the replay machine

An NDTM run along a choice word is a deterministic run that reads the word from a tape: the
**replay machine** `Turing.NDTM.replayTM N` has one extra work tape, the *choice tape*, which it
reads at every step (a blank reads as `false`) to select the transition function, moving the
choice head right and never writing it. The replay lemma `Turing.NDTM.replayTM_runFrom`
identifies its runs with `N`'s branches. This is the certificate view of nondeterminism
([AB09, §2.1.2, Theorem 2.6]: the choices of an accepting branch are a certificate that a
deterministic verifier checks by simulation).

## Design

* **No new machinery is needed to interpret nondeterministic codes.** A coded NDTM's replay
  machine is a deterministic three-work-tape machine, so its fixed `k`-record serialization
  (`Turing.serializeK`) is interpreted by the deterministic step block (host H2) at `k = 3`,
  unchanged (user decision 3 of 2026-10-13; the C1 design note §3.2, option (c)).
* **Consumers:** the per-code replay canonizer and the interpreter core
  (`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.NDCodeSimulator`) and the exhaustive replay
  (`TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.ExhaustiveReplay`). It can also replace the private choice-word
  replay of `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.Nondeterminism` (the C1 design note §3.5, inferred).

## Main definitions

* `Turing.NDTM.replayTM` — the replay machine. [AB09, §2.1.2]
* `Turing.NDTM.withChoiceTape` — an NDTM configuration extended by a choice tape.

## Main results

* `Turing.NDTM.replayTM_runFrom` — the replay lemma (proved).
* The fields of the replay machine `Turing.NDTM.replayTM_q₀`, `_tr` and of the extended
  configuration `Turing.NDTM.withChoiceTape_state`, `_inputPos`, `_workTapes`, `_workTapePos`,
  `_output` (the ND inventory API, C1's pre-ship inventory, 2026-10-17).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§2.1.2, Theorem 2.6 and its proof.)
-/

namespace Turing.NDTM

variable {k : ℕ} {S : Type*}

/-- **The replay machine** of an NDTM `N` with `k` work tapes: the deterministic machine with
`k + 1` work tapes that, at every step, reads the choice tape (the last one; a blank reads as
`false`), applies the corresponding transition function of `N` to the first `k` tapes, and
moves the choice head one cell right without writing it. Its states, initial state, input moves
and output are `N`'s. [AB09, §2.1.2: a branch of an NDTM is its run along a choice word; the
verifier of Theorem 2.6 reads that word] -/
def replayTM (N : NDTM k Bool S) : MultiTapeTM (k + 1) Bool S where
  q₀ := N.q₀
  tr := fun q inp w =>
    let a := N.tr ((w (Fin.last k)).getD false) q inp (fun i => w i.castSucc)
    ⟨a.inputTape, Fin.lastCases (none, 1) a.workTapes, a.output, a.state⟩

/-! The replay machine's fields as equations (the ND inventory API, 2026-10-17), by `simps` without
the `simp` attribute: `N.replayTM.q₀ = N.q₀`, and `N.replayTM.tr q inp w` is the action of
`N.tr ((w (Fin.last k)).getD false) q inp (fun i => w i.castSucc)` on the first `k` tapes, with the
choice tape unwritten and its head moved right. -/
attribute [simps (config := { isSimp := false }) q₀ tr] replayTM

/-- The configuration `c` of an NDTM extended by a choice tape `ct` with its head at `cp` as the
last work tape; every other field is `c`'s. -/
def withChoiceTape {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (ct : ℤ → Option Bool) (cp : ℤ) :
    Cfg (k + 1) Bool S x :=
  ⟨c.state, c.inputPos, Fin.lastCases ct c.workTapes, Fin.lastCases cp c.workTapePos, c.output⟩

/-! The extended configuration's fields as equations (the ND inventory API, 2026-10-17), by `simps`
without the `simp` attribute: the state, input head and output are `c`'s, and
`(withChoiceTape c ct cp).workTapes = Fin.lastCases ct c.workTapes`,
`(withChoiceTape c ct cp).workTapePos = Fin.lastCases cp c.workTapePos`. -/
attribute [simps (config := { isSimp := false }) state inputPos workTapes workTapePos output]
  withChoiceTape

/-- **The replay lemma.** With the word `s` on the choice tape from cell `0`, the replay
machine's run for `t ≤ |s|` steps is the NDTM's branch along `s.take t`, extended by the
unchanged choice tape, with the choice head at some `p ≤ t`, and at exactly `t` while that
branch is live (the head stops when the branch halts). [AB09, §2.1.2]

**Proof sketch.** Induct on `t`. A live step reads `s[t]` under the choice head at `t`, so the
replay machine applies `N.tr s[t]` to the first `k` tapes and moves the choice head; a halted
step is the identity on both sides (`Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt`). -/
theorem replayTM_runFrom {x : List Bool} (N : NDTM k Bool S) (c : Cfg k Bool S x)
    (s : List Bool) (t : ℕ) (ht : t ≤ s.length) :
    ∃ p ≤ t, ((N.runWith (s.take t) c).state ≠ none → p = t) ∧
      N.replayTM.runFrom (withChoiceTape c (FinTM.bufferTape s) 0) t =
        withChoiceTape (N.runWith (s.take t) c) (FinTM.bufferTape s) p := by
  induction t with
  | zero => exact ⟨0, le_rfl, fun _ => rfl, rfl⟩
  | succ t ih =>
    obtain ⟨p, hp, hlive, hrun⟩ := ih (by omega)
    have htake : s.take (t + 1) = s.take t ++ [s[t]'(by omega)] :=
      List.take_succ_eq_append_getElem (by omega)
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', hrun, htake, runWith_append]
    cases hs : (N.runWith (s.take t) c).state with
    | none =>
      refine ⟨p, by omega, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro h
        exact absurd (by rw [runWith_of_halt _ hs]; exact hs) h
      · rw [runWith_of_halt _ hs]
        exact MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt (by simp [withChoiceTape, hs])
    | some q =>
      have hpt : p = t := hlive (by simp [hs])
      subst hpt
      refine ⟨p + 1, le_rfl, fun _ => rfl, ?_⟩
      set e := N.runWith (s.take p) c with he
      have hread : (withChoiceTape e (FinTM.bufferTape s) (p : ℤ)).workTapeSymbols
          (Fin.last k) = some (s[p]'(by omega)) := by
        simp [withChoiceTape, Cfg.workTapeSymbols, FinTM.bufferTape]
      have hwork : (fun i : Fin k =>
          (withChoiceTape e (FinTM.bufferTape s) (p : ℤ)).workTapeSymbols i.castSucc) =
          e.workTapeSymbols := by
        funext i
        simp [withChoiceTape, Cfg.workTapeSymbols]
      have hinp : (withChoiceTape e (FinTM.bufferTape s) (p : ℤ)).inputSymbol =
          e.inputSymbol := rfl
      unfold MultiTapeTM.step
      have hst : (withChoiceTape e (FinTM.bufferTape s) (p : ℤ)).state = some q := by
        simp [withChoiceTape, hs]
      rw [hst]
      simp only [runWith_cons, runWith_nil]
      unfold stepWith
      rw [hs]
      simp only [replayTM]
      rw [hread, hwork, hinp]
      simp only [Option.getD_some]
      apply Cfg.ext
      · rfl
      · rfl
      · funext j
        refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun i => ?_) j
        · simp [withChoiceTape, Action.apply]
        · simp [withChoiceTape, Action.apply]
      · funext j
        refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun i => ?_) j
        · simp [withChoiceTape, Action.apply]
        · simp [withChoiceTape, Action.apply]
      · rfl

end Turing.NDTM
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/CfgFacts.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.StateRenaming

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Elementary facts about configurations

Four small facts that machine constructions over several phases use repeatedly: the input read
depends on the input head only; a live configuration redirected to a state of phase `i` is the
tagged configuration of phase `i`; a configuration tagged by one phase is never at a state of
another; and a list of equal-length chunks has the expected length.

## Main definitions

No new definitions.

## Main results

* `Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol_congr` — configurations whose input heads agree read the same input
  symbol, across machines.
* `Turing.Cfg.mapState_eq_of_fields` — a renamed configuration is any configuration with its four
  data fields and the renamed state.
* `Turing.Cfg.mapState_const_eq_mapState_sigma` — redirecting a live configuration to `⟨i, q⟩`
  gives phase `i`'s tagged configuration at `q`.
* `Turing.Cfg.mapState_sigma_state_ne` — a configuration tagged by phase `i` is at no state of
  another phase.
* `Turing.length_flatMap_uniform` — a list of equal-length chunks has length count × chunk length.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2, Turing machines and their configurations.)
-/

namespace Turing

/-- **The input read depends on the input head only.** Two configurations on the same input,
of machines with any numbers of work tapes and any states, read the same input symbol when their
input heads are at the same position.

**Proof sketch.** At position `0` and at `|input| + 1` both read blank
(`Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol_of_zero`, `Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol_of_end`); at an inner position `1 + p`
both read `input[p]` (`Turing.inputSymbolInner`). -/
theorem Cfg.inputSymbol_congr {Symbol : Type*} {k k' : ℕ} {S S' : Type*} {input : List Symbol}
    (c : Cfg k Symbol S input) (c' : Cfg k' Symbol S' input)
    (h : c.inputPos.val = c'.inputPos.val) : c.inputSymbol = c'.inputSymbol := by
  by_cases h0 : c.inputPos.val = 0
  · have h0' : c'.inputPos = 0 := Fin.ext (by rw [← h]; exact h0)
    rw [Cfg.inputSymbol_of_zero (Fin.ext h0), Cfg.inputSymbol_of_zero h0']
  · by_cases he : c.inputPos.val = input.length + 1
    · rw [Cfg.inputSymbol_of_end he, Cfg.inputSymbol_of_end (by omega)]
    · have hlt := c.inputPos.isLt
      rw [inputSymbolInner (c.inputPos.val - 1) (by omega) (by omega),
        inputSymbolInner (cfg := c') (c.inputPos.val - 1) (by omega) (by omega)]

/-- **A renamed configuration, field by field.** Renaming the states of `c` by `f` gives any
configuration `d` that has `c`'s input head, tapes, work heads and output and whose state is `c`'s
state renamed.

**Proof sketch.** Compare the five fields through the state-renaming equations
(`Turing.Cfg.mapState_state` and the others). -/
theorem Cfg.mapState_eq_of_fields {k : ℕ} {Γ S S' : Type*} {x : List Γ} (c : Cfg k Γ S x)
    (f : S → S') (d : Cfg k Γ S' x) (hs : c.state.map f = d.state) (hi : c.inputPos = d.inputPos)
    (hw : c.workTapes = d.workTapes) (hp : c.workTapePos = d.workTapePos)
    (ho : c.output = d.output) : c.mapState f = d := by
  apply Cfg.ext
  · rw [Cfg.mapState_state, hs]
  · rw [Cfg.mapState_inputPos, hi]
  · funext j p; rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapes, hw]
  · funext j; rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapePos, hp]
  · rw [Cfg.mapState_output, ho]

/-- **Redirecting a live configuration to a phase's state.** If `c` is live and `c₂` is a
configuration of phase `i` at state `q` with `c`'s tapes, heads and output, then sending every
state of `c` to `⟨i, q⟩` gives `c₂` tagged by `i`.

**Proof sketch.** Both sides are renamings; by `Turing.Cfg.mapState_eq_of_fields` it suffices to
compare the left side's fields with the right side's: the states are both `some ⟨i, q⟩` since `c`
is live, and the remaining fields are the hypotheses. -/
theorem Cfg.mapState_const_eq_mapState_sigma {k : ℕ} {Γ I S : Type*} {Ph : I → Type*}
    {x : List Γ} {i : I} (c : Cfg k Γ S x) (c₂ : Cfg k Γ (Ph i) x) {q : Ph i}
    (hc : c.state.isSome) (hstate : c₂.state = some q) (hin : c.inputPos = c₂.inputPos)
    (hw : c.workTapes = c₂.workTapes) (hp : c.workTapePos = c₂.workTapePos)
    (ho : c.output = c₂.output) :
    c.mapState (fun _ => (⟨i, q⟩ : Σ j, Ph j)) = c₂.mapState (Sigma.mk i) := by
  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := Option.isSome_iff_exists.mp hc
  refine Cfg.mapState_eq_of_fields c _ _ ?_ (by rw [Cfg.mapState_inputPos, hin])
    (by funext j p; rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapes, hw])
    (by funext j; rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapePos, hp]) (by rw [Cfg.mapState_output, ho])
  rw [Cfg.mapState_state, hs, hstate, Option.map_some, Option.map_some]

/-- **A tagged configuration is at no other phase's state.** A configuration tagged by phase `i`
(its states sent into the sum by `Sigma.mk i`) is never at a state `v` of a phase `v.1 ≠ i`. -/
theorem Cfg.mapState_sigma_state_ne {k : ℕ} {Γ I : Type*} {Ph : I → Type*} {x : List Γ}
    (i : I) (v : Σ j, Ph j) (hi : i ≠ v.1) (c : Cfg k Γ (Ph i) x) :
    (c.mapState (Sigma.mk i)).state ≠ some v := by
  rw [Cfg.mapState_state]
  cases hs : c.state with
  | none => exact Option.noConfusion
  | some s =>
    intro h
    exact hi (congrArg Sigma.fst (Option.some.inj h))

/-- **Equal-length chunks.** If every chunk `f a` has length `c`, the concatenation of the chunks
of a list `l` has length `|l| · c`. -/
theorem length_flatMap_uniform {α β : Type*} (l : List α) (f : α → List β) {c : ℕ}
    (hf : ∀ a, (f a).length = c) : (l.flatMap f).length = l.length * c := by
  rw [List.length_flatMap, List.map_congr_left (fun a _ => hf a), List.map_const',
    List.sum_replicate]
  rfl

end Turing
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/BufferWords.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Buffer tapes of composite words

Cell identities for the buffer tape `Turing.FinTM.bufferTape w`, which holds the word `w` from
cell `0` and is blank everywhere else, when `w` is built from smaller words: a suffix read at an
offset, a middle word's letters, a prefix or a suffix of the word, the blank cells off the word,
and the cells of a unary word with its terminator. A machine's contract can then read the fields
of a serialized layout, such as a pair encoding followed by a unary state and a table, cell by
cell. Every proof reads `bufferTape` only through its published equations.

## Main results

* `Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append_shift` — past a prefix `u`, the buffer of `u ++ w` reads `w`'s
  buffer.
* `Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append_mid` — the letters of the middle word of `u ++ w ++ v`.
* `Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_drop`, `Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_take` — the buffer of a suffix or a
  prefix of a word.
* `Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_eq_none_of_not_mem` — every cell off the word is blank.
* `Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_unary` — the cells of the unary word `1^q 0`, its terminator
  included.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2: tapes holding words; §1.4: encodings of machines as
  strings, whose fields these identities read.)
-/

namespace Turing.FinTM

/-- **A suffix at an offset**: at a cell `z ≥ 0` past the prefix `u`, the buffer of `u ++ w`
reads the buffer of `w` at `z`, including `w`'s right blank and every cell beyond it.

**Proof sketch.** Both cells are nonnegative, and list lookup in `u ++ w` at `|u| + z` is lookup
in `w` at `z`. -/
theorem bufferTape_append_shift {Symbol : Type*} (u w : List Symbol) {z : ℤ} (hz : 0 ≤ z) :
    bufferTape (u ++ w) (u.length + z) = bufferTape w z := by
  rw [bufferTape_eq, bufferTape_eq, if_pos (by omega), if_pos hz,
    show ((u.length : ℤ) + z).toNat = u.length + z.toNat by omega,
    List.getElem?_append_right (Nat.le_add_right _ _), Nat.add_sub_cancel_left]

/-- **A middle word's letters**: in the buffer of `u ++ w ++ v`, the cell `|u| + r` holds `w`'s
letter `r`, for `r < |w|`.

**Proof sketch.** Past `u`, the buffer reads the buffer of `w ++ v`
(`Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append_shift`), whose cell `r < |w|` is `w`'s letter. -/
theorem bufferTape_append_mid {Symbol : Type*} (u w v : List Symbol) (r : ℕ) (hr : r < w.length) :
    bufferTape (u ++ w ++ v) (u.length + r) = some w[r] := by
  rw [List.append_assoc, bufferTape_append_shift u (w ++ v) (Int.natCast_nonneg r), bufferTape_nat,
    List.getElem?_append_left hr, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hr]

/-- **The buffer of a suffix**: at a cell `z ≥ 0`, the buffer of `w.drop r` reads the buffer of
`w` at `r + z`.

**Proof sketch.** `w` is `w.take r ++ w.drop r`. If `r ≤ |w|`, the prefix has length `r` and
`Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append_shift` applies. Otherwise the suffix is empty, and the cell
`r + z` is past `w`'s end, so both sides are blank. -/
theorem bufferTape_drop {Symbol : Type*} (w : List Symbol) (r : ℕ) {z : ℤ} (hz : 0 ≤ z) :
    bufferTape (w.drop r) z = bufferTape w (r + z) := by
  by_cases hr : r ≤ w.length
  · have h := bufferTape_append_shift (w.take r) (w.drop r) hz
    rw [List.take_append_drop, List.length_take, min_eq_left hr] at h
    exact h.symm
  · rw [List.drop_eq_nil_of_le (by omega), bufferTape_eq, bufferTape_eq, if_pos hz,
      if_pos (by omega), List.getElem?_nil, List.getElem?_eq_none (by omega)]

/-- **The buffer of a prefix**: at a cell `z < n`, the buffer of `w.take n` reads the buffer of
`w`.

**Proof sketch.** Negative cells are blank on both sides. At `0 ≤ z < n`, list lookup in
`w.take n` is lookup in `w`. -/
theorem bufferTape_take {Symbol : Type*} (w : List Symbol) (n : ℕ) {z : ℤ} (hz : z < n) :
    bufferTape (w.take n) z = bufferTape w z := by
  rw [bufferTape_eq, bufferTape_eq]
  split_ifs with h
  · rw [List.getElem?_take, if_pos (by omega)]
  · rfl

/-- **Off the word, the buffer is blank**: every cell outside `[0, |w|)` reads `none`.

**Proof sketch.** A negative cell is blank by the buffer's equation, and a cell at or past `|w|`
is past the end of the list. -/
theorem bufferTape_eq_none_of_not_mem {Symbol : Type*} (w : List Symbol) {z : ℤ}
    (hz : ¬(0 ≤ z ∧ z < w.length)) : bufferTape w z = none := by
  rw [bufferTape_eq]
  split_ifs with h
  · exact List.getElem?_eq_none (by omega)
  · rfl

/-- **A unary word's cells**: the buffer of `1^q 0` (`q` letters `true`, then the terminator
`false`) reads `true` at the cells `r < q` and `false` at `r = q`, that is,
`some (decide (r < q))` for every `r ≤ q`.

**Proof sketch.** At `r < q` list lookup stays in the block of `true`s; at `r = q` it reads the
terminator. -/
theorem bufferTape_unary (q r : ℕ) (hr : r ≤ q) :
    bufferTape (List.replicate q true ++ [false]) r = some (decide (r < q)) := by
  rw [bufferTape_nat]
  by_cases hlt : r < q
  · rw [List.getElem?_append_left (by rw [List.length_replicate]; exact hlt),
      List.getElem?_replicate_of_lt hlt, decide_eq_true hlt]
  · obtain rfl : r = q := by omega
    rw [List.getElem?_append_right (by rw [List.length_replicate]), List.length_replicate,
      Nat.sub_self, decide_eq_false (Nat.lt_irrefl r)]
    rfl

end Turing.FinTM
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassNP.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTime
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimePairing
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.Transducer
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.CounterProgPolyTime
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimePrefix
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.NP
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.CoNP
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PClosure
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.EXP
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.ExpPoly
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.Reductions
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.NTIME
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.Nondeterminism
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.ExhaustiveReplay
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.NDNormalForm
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.SAT
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.TMSAT
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.Tautology

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Complexity — NP and NP-completeness

The classes and reduction notions of [AB09, ch. 2] (see
`AroraBarakChapter2Plan.md` for the chapter-level plan).

## Contents

* `PolyTime` — polynomial bounds and polynomial-time computable functions (FP),
  with the closure calculus reductions assemble with [AB09, §2.2].
* `PolyTimePairing` — closure of FP under pairing (`x ↦ ⟨f x, g x⟩`), mapping the
  second pair component, constants, `x ↦ 1^|x|`, concatenation, the total pair
  projections, Boolean branching and length tests.
* `Transducer` — one-pass transducers (Mealy machines) run in linear time.
* `CounterProgPolyTime` — counter programs halting in polynomially many steps compute
  polynomial-time functions.
* `PolyTimePrefix` — take or drop a prefix of a pair's second component at the
  length of its first component, in polynomial time.
* `NP` — the class `NP` via polynomial-time verifiers [AB09, Definition 2.1]
  and the bounded-length certificate variant [AB09, Exercise 2.1].
* `CoNP` — the class `coNP`, its ∀-certificate characterization
  [AB09, Definitions 2.19-2.20], and `P`'s closure under complement.
* `PClosure` — closure of `P` under polynomial-time preimages, Boolean operations and
  Boolean functions of finitely many tests.
* `EXP` — the classes `EXP` and `NEXP` and the containment chain
  [AB09, Claim 2.4, §2.6.2].
* `ExpPoly` — exponential-polynomial time bounds `2^{K(n+1)^k}` and their closure
  properties; such bounds give `EXP`.
* `Reductions` — Karp reductions, `NP`-hardness and `NP`-completeness
  [AB09, Definition 2.7, Theorem 2.8], and `HALT`'s status
  [AB09, Exercise 2.8].
* `NTIME` — nondeterministic deciding and the classes `NTIME`
  [AB09, §2.1.2, Definition 2.5] (the machine model lives in
  `TuringMachine/Nondeterministic`).
* `Nondeterminism` — the `NTIME` characterizations of `NP` [AB09, Theorem 2.6] and
  `NEXP` [AB09, §2.6.2], and the padding theorem [AB09, Theorem 2.22].
* `ExhaustiveReplay` — the exhaustive replay of a fixed NDTM: acceptance decided
  deterministically within `C·2^{C·(T + 1)}` wherever every branch halts within `T`
  [AB09, §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.2], and `BF := E(UN)` for the hierarchy.
* `NDNormalForm` — the linear-overhead coded normal form: every bundled binary NDTM has a
  coded two-work-tape equivalent whose acceptance tracks its own, forward within a linear
  allowance and backward unboundedly [AB09, §3.2]; the time hierarchy diagonalizes over
  these codes. The normal form is sorried.
* `SAT` — the languages `SAT` and `3SAT`, their membership in `NP`, and
  `SAT ≤ₚ 3SAT` [AB09, §2.3.1, Theorem 2.10 (membership), Lemma 2.14] (the
  formula layer lives in `TCSlib.Complexity.Formulas`).
* `TMSAT` — the generic `NP`-complete language [AB09, Theorem 2.9], with the
  polynomial time-constructibility support statement.
* `Tautology` — `coNP`-hardness/completeness and `TAUTOLOGY` on the DNF
  fragment [AB09, §2.6.1, Example 2.21].
-/
```
